verses.1:1: Now it came to pass after the death of Joshua that the children of Israel inquired of the Lord, saying, "Who shall go up for us against the Canaanites as leader, to make war against them?"
verses.1:2: And the Lord said, "Judah shall go up; behold, I have given the land into his hand."
verses.1:3: Then Judah said to Simeon his brother, "Come up with me into my lot, and let us do battle against the Canaanites; and I also will go with you into your lot." So Simeon went with him.
verses.1:4: And Judah went up, and the Lord delivered the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hands; and they cut them down in Bezek, as many as ten thousand men.
verses.1:5: And they came upon Adoni-Bezek in Bezek and arrayed themselves in battle against him, and they struck down the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
verses.1:6: Then Adoni-Bezek fled, and they pursued after him and captured him, and cut off the extremities of his hands and the extremities of his feet.
verses.1:7: And Adoni-Bezek said, "Seventy kings, having the extremities of their hands and the extremities of their feet cut off, used to gather what fell beneath my table; therefore, just as I have done, so God has repaid me." And they brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.
verses.1:8: Now the children of Judah fought against Jerusalem, and captured it, and struck it with the edge of the sword, and set the city ablaze with fire.
verses.1:9: And afterward the children of Judah went down to make war against the Canaanites who dwelt in the hill country, and in the south, and in the lowland.
verses.1:10: Then Judah marched against the Canaanites who dwelt in Hebron, and Hebron came out to meet them—now the name of Hebron formerly was Kariarboxepher—and they struck down Sheshai, and Achinaan, and Talmai, the offspring of Anak.
verses.1:11: And from there they went up against the inhabitants of Debir; now the name of Debir formerly was Kiriath-sepher, the City of Letters.
verses.1:12: And Caleb said, "Whoever strikes the City of Letters and captures it, to him I will give Aza my daughter as a wife."
verses.1:13: And Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's brother, the younger, captured it; and Caleb gave him Aza his daughter as a wife.
verses.1:14: Now it came to pass upon her arrival that Othniel urged her to ask her father for a field. And she murmured and cried out from the donkey, "Into a land of the south you have given me away!" And Caleb said to her, "What is the matter with you?"
verses.1:15: And Achsah said to him, "Give me a blessing, for into a land of the south you have given me away; you shall also give me a redemption of water." So Caleb gave her according to her heart the redemption of the upper places and the redemption of the lower places.
verses.1:16: Now the children of Jethro the Kenite, the father-in-law of Moses, went up from the City of Palms with the children of Judah into the wilderness that is in the south of Judah, which is at the descent of Arad; and they dwelt with the people.
verses.1:17: Then Judah went with Simeon his brother, and struck down the Canaanites who dwelt in Sephek, and utterly destroyed them; and he called the name of the city Anathema.
verses.1:18: And Judah did not inherit Gaza nor its borders, nor Ashkelon nor its borders, nor Ekron nor its borders, nor Ashdod nor its surrounding lands.
verses.1:19: And the Lord was with Judah, and he inherited the hill country, for they were not able to utterly destroy the inhabitants of the valley, because Rechab had given orders to them.
verses.1:20: And they gave Hebron to Caleb, just as Moses had spoken; and from there he inherited the three cities of the sons of Anak.
verses.1:21: Yet the children of Benjamin did not dispossess the Jebusites who dwelt in Jerusalem; so the Jebusites have dwelt with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem to this day.
verses.1:22: Now the children of Joseph, they also went up against Bethel, and the Lord was with them.
verses.1:23: And they encamped and spied out Bethel; now the name of their city formerly was Luz.
verses.1:24: And the watchmen looked, and behold, a man was coming out of the city; and they took him and said to him, "Show us the entrance to the city, and we will show mercy to you."
verses.1:25: So he showed them the entrance to the city, and they struck the city with the edge of the sword; but the man and his kindred they sent away.
verses.1:26: And the man went to the land of the Hittites, and built a city there, and called its name Luz; that is its name to this day.
verses.1:27: Moreover, Manasseh did not remove Beth-shan, which is the City of the Scythians, nor its daughters nor its surrounding towns, nor Taanach nor its daughters, nor the inhabitants of Dor nor its daughters, nor the inhabitants of Balak nor its surrounding towns nor its daughters, nor the inhabitants of Megiddo nor its surrounding towns nor its daughters, nor the inhabitants of Ibleam nor its surrounding towns nor its daughters; and the Canaanites began to dwell in that land.
verses.1:28: And it came to pass, when Israel grew strong, that they put the Canaanites under tribute, and did not utterly remove them.
verses.1:29: And Ephraim did not remove the Canaanites who dwelt in Gezer; so the Canaanites dwelt in his midst in Gezer and became subject to tribute.
verses.1:30: And Zebulun did not remove the inhabitants of Kedron nor the inhabitants of Domana; so the Canaanites dwelt in their midst and became subject to tribute to them.
verses.1:31: And Asher did not remove the inhabitants of Acco—and it became subject to tribute to him—nor the inhabitants of Dor, nor the inhabitants of Sidon, nor the inhabitants of Dalaph, nor Aschazi, nor Chebda, nor Naei, nor Ereo.
verses.1:32: So Asher dwelt in the midst of the Canaanites who inhabited the land, because he was not able to remove them.
verses.1:33: And Naphtali did not remove the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh nor the inhabitants of Beth-anach; so Naphtali dwelt in the midst of the Canaanites who inhabited the land, and the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and of Beth-anath became subject to tribute to them.
verses.1:34: And the Amorites pressed the children of Dan into the hill country, for they did not allow them to come down into the valley.
verses.1:35: And the Amorites began to dwell in the potsherd mountain, in which are the bears and in which are the foxes, in Myrsinon and in Thalabin; yet the hand of the house of Joseph grew heavy upon the Amorites, and they became subject to tribute to them.
verses.1:36: And the border of the Amorites was from the Ascent of Akrabbim, from the Rock and upward.
verses.2:1: Now the Angel of the Lord went up from Gilgal to the Place of Weeping, and to Bethel, and to the house of Israel, and said to them, "Thus says the Lord: I brought you up out of Egypt, and brought you into the land which I swore to your fathers; and I said, 'I will never break My covenant with you,
verses.2:2: and you shall make no covenant with those who dwell in this land, nor shall you worship their gods, but you shall shatter their carved images and tear down their altars.' Yet you have not obeyed My voice, because you have done these things.
verses.2:3: Therefore I also said, 'I will by no means remove them from before you; and they shall be for distresses to you, and their gods shall be a snare to you.'"
verses.2:4: And it came to pass, when the Angel of the Lord spoke these words to all the children of Israel, that the people lifted up their voice and wept.
verses.2:5: And they named the name of that place Places of Weeping; and they sacrificed there to the Lord.
verses.2:6: Now Joshua sent the people away, and each man went to his own inheritance to possess the land.
verses.2:7: And the people served the Lord all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who lived long after Joshua, who knew all the great work of the Lord which He had done in Israel.
verses.2:8: And Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died, being one hundred and ten years old.
verses.2:9: And they buried him within the border of his inheritance in Timnath-heres, in the hill country of Ephraim, on the north side of Mount Gaash.
verses.2:10: And all that generation also was gathered to their fathers; and another generation arose after them who did not know the Lord nor the work which He had done in Israel.
verses.2:11: Then the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, and served the Baals.
verses.2:12: And they forsook the Lord, the God of their fathers, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt; and they walked after other gods from among the gods of the nations that were all around them, and worshiped them; and they provoked the Lord to anger.
verses.2:13: And they forsook Him, and served Baal and the Ashtoreths.
verses.2:14: And the Lord was incensed with wrath against Israel, and delivered them into the hands of plunderers, and they plundered them; and He sold them into the hands of their enemies all around, so that they could no longer stand before the face of their enemies in all places wherever they went out.
verses.2:15: And the hand of the Lord was against them for calamity, just as the Lord had spoken, and just as the Lord had sworn to them; and He afflicted them exceedingly.
verses.2:16: Then the Lord raised up judges, and the Lord saved them out of the hand of those who plundered them. Yet they did not even obey the judges,
verses.2:17: for they played the harlot after other gods and worshiped them; and they turned aside quickly from the way in which their fathers had walked, in obeying the words of the Lord; they did not do so.
verses.2:18: And whenever the Lord raised up judges for them, the Lord was with the judge and saved them out of the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge; for the Lord was moved with compassion by their groaning because of those who besieged them and afflicted them.
verses.2:19: Yet it came to pass, when the judge died, that they turned back and again acted more corruptly than their fathers, to walk after other gods, to serve them and worship them; they did not cast away their practices nor their stubborn ways.
verses.2:20: Then the Lord was incensed with wrath against Israel, and He said, "Because this nation has forsaken My covenant which I commanded their fathers, and has not obeyed My voice,
verses.2:21: I also will no longer remove a single man from before them of the nations which Joshua the son of Nun left in the land." And He left them
verses.2:22: to test Israel by them, whether they keep the way of the Lord to walk in it, in the manner that their fathers kept it, or not.
verses.2:23: Therefore the Lord will leave these nations, so as not to remove them quickly; and He did not deliver them into the hand of Joshua.
verses.3:1: Now these are the nations which the Lord left behind so as to test Israel by them, all those who had not known the wars of Canaan,
verses.3:2: only for the sake of the generations of the children of Israel, to teach them war—except that those before them had not known these things:
verses.3:3: the five satrapies of the foreigners, and all the Canaanites, and the Sidonians, and the Hivites who dwelt in Lebanon, from Mount Hermon as far as Lebo-hamath.
verses.3:4: And it came to pass so as to test Israel by them, to know whether they would heed the commandments of the Lord, which He commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.
verses.3:5: Thus the children of Israel dwelt in the midst of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
verses.3:6: And they took their daughters for themselves as wives, and gave their own daughters to their sons; and they served their gods.
verses.3:7: So the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, and forgot the Lord their God, and served the Baals and the groves.
verses.3:8: Therefore the Lord was incensed with wrath against Israel, and He sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim, king of the rivers of Syria; and the children of Israel served Cushan-rishathaim eight years.
verses.3:9: And the children of Israel cried out to the Lord; and the Lord raised up a savior for Israel, and he saved them—Othniel the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, who was younger than he.
verses.3:10: And the Spirit of the Lord came upon him, and he judged Israel. And he went out to war against Cushan-rishathaim; and the Lord delivered Cushan-rishathaim, king of Syria of the rivers, into his hand, and his hand prevailed over Cushan-rishathaim.
verses.3:11: And the land had rest forty years; and Othniel the son of Kenaz died.
verses.3:12: And the children of Israel again did evil before the Lord; and the Lord strengthened Eglon, king of Moab, against Israel, because they had done evil in the sight of the Lord.
verses.3:13: And he gathered to himself all the children of Ammon and Amalek, and went and struck Israel, and took possession of the City of Palms.
verses.3:14: And the children of Israel served Eglon, king of Moab, eighteen years.
verses.3:15: And the children of Israel cried out to the Lord; and He raised up for them a savior, Ehud the son of Gera, the son of Jemini, an ambidextrous man. And the children of Israel sent gifts by his hand to Eglon, king of Moab.
verses.3:16: And Ehud made for himself a two-edged dagger, a span in length, and girded it under his cloak upon his right thigh.
verses.3:17: And he went and presented the gifts to Eglon, king of Moab; now Eglon was a very handsome man.
verses.3:18: And it came to pass, when Ehud had finished presenting the gifts, that he sent away those who carried the gifts.
verses.3:19: But he himself turned back from the carved images that were near Gilgal, and Ehud said, "I have a secret word for you, O king." And Eglon said to him, "Keep silence!" And he sent away from himself all those who stood in attendance upon him.
verses.3:20: And Ehud came in to him; and he was sitting in his own summer upper chamber, entirely alone. And Ehud said, "I have a word from God for you, O king." And Eglon rose up from the throne near him.
verses.3:21: And it came to pass, at the very moment he rose up, that Ehud stretched out his left hand and took the dagger from upon his right thigh and thrust it into his belly;
verses.3:22: and he drove in the hilt also after the blade; and the fat closed over the blade, for he did not draw the dagger out of his belly.
verses.3:23: And Ehud went out through the porch, and passed out past those stationed on guard, and shut the doors of the upper chamber upon him, and bolted them.
verses.3:24: And when he had gone out, his servants came and looked, and behold, the doors of the upper chamber were bolted; and they said, "Could he perhaps be relieving himself in the summer chamber?"
verses.3:25: So they waited until they were ashamed; and behold, there was no one opening the doors of the upper chamber. Therefore they took the key and opened them, and behold, their lord had fallen upon the ground, dead.
verses.3:26: Now Ehud escaped while they were in confusion, and there was no one paying attention to him; and he passed beyond the carved images and escaped to Seteirotha.
verses.3:27: And it came to pass, when Ehud came into the land of Israel, that he blew the horn in Mount Ephraim; and the children of Israel went down with him from the mountain, and he was before them.
verses.3:28: And he said to them, "Go down after me, for the Lord God has delivered our enemies, Moab, into our hand." So they went down after him, and seized the fords of the Jordan belonging to Moab, and he did not allow a man to cross over.
verses.3:29: And they struck down of Moab on that day about ten thousand men, every stout man and every man of valor; and not a man escaped.
verses.3:30: So Moab was humbled on that day under the hand of Israel, and the land had rest eighty years; and Ehud judged them until he died.
verses.3:31: And after him arose Shamgar the son of Deinach, and he struck down the foreigners, to the number of six hundred men, with the plowshare of the oxen; and he also saved Israel.
verses.4:1: And the children of Israel again did evil before the Lord; and Ehud had died.
verses.4:2: And the Lord sold the children of Israel into the hand of Jabin, king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor; and the commander of his army was Sisera, and he dwelt in Harosheth of the Nations.
verses.4:3: And the children of Israel cried out to the Lord, for he had nine hundred chariots of iron, and he oppressed Israel with harsh force for twenty years.
verses.4:4: Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, was judging Israel at that time.
verses.4:5: And she sat beneath the palm tree of Deborah between Bama and Bethel in Mount Ephraim; and the children of Israel went up to her for judgment.
verses.4:6: And Deborah sent and called Barak the son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali, and said to him, "Has not the Lord, the God of Israel, commanded you: 'You shall go to Mount Tabor, and take with you ten thousand men of the sons of Naphtali and of the sons of Zebulun,
verses.4:7: and I will bring to you at the brook Kishon Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, and his chariots and his multitude, and I will deliver him into your hands'?"
verses.4:8: And Barak said to her, "If you go with me, I will go; and if you do not go, I will not go, for I do not know the day on which the Lord prospers the angel with me."
verses.4:9: And she said, "I will surely go with you; nevertheless, know that the honor shall not be yours on the way that you are going, for into the hand of a woman the Lord will sell Sisera." And Deborah arose and went with Barak from Kedesh.
verses.4:10: And Barak summoned Zebulun and Naphtali from Kedesh, and ten thousand men went up at his feet; and Deborah went up with him.
verses.4:11: Now Heber the Kenite had separated himself from Kain, from the sons of Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses, and pitched his tent as far as the oak of the covetous, which is next to Kedesh.
verses.4:12: And it was reported to Sisera that Barak the son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor.
verses.4:13: And Sisera summoned all his chariots, nine hundred chariots of iron, and all the people who were with him, from Harosheth of the Nations to the brook Kishon.
verses.4:14: And Deborah said to Barak, "Arise, for this is the day in which the Lord has delivered Sisera into your hand; for the Lord shall go out before you." So Barak went down from Mount Tabor, with ten thousand men behind him.
verses.4:15: And the Lord threw Sisera and all his chariots and all his army into panic by the edge of the sword before Barak; and Sisera got down from his chariot and fled on foot.
verses.4:16: And Barak pursued after the chariots and after the army as far as Harosheth of the Nations; and the entire army of Sisera fell by the edge of the sword—not even one was left.
verses.4:17: Now Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the companion, the Kenite, for there was peace between Jabin, king of Hazor, and the house of Heber the Kenite.
verses.4:18: And Jael went out to meet Sisera and said to him, "Turn aside, my lord, turn aside to me; do not fear." And he turned aside to her into the tent; and she covered him with a blanket.
verses.4:19: And Sisera said to her, "Please give me a little water to drink, for I am thirsty." So she opened the skin of milk and gave him a drink, and covered him.
verses.4:20: And Sisera said to her, "Please stand at the door of the tent, and it shall be that if any man comes to you and inquires of you and says, 'Is there a man here?' then you shall say, 'There is not.'"
verses.4:21: Then Jael, the wife of Heber, took the tent peg and put the hammer in her hand, and went in to him secretly and drove the peg into his temple, and it went right through into the ground; and he, stunned, fainted away and died.
verses.4:22: And behold, Barak was pursuing Sisera; and Jael went out to meet him and said to him, "Come, and I will show you the man whom you seek." And he went in to her, and behold, Sisera lay prostrate, dead, with the peg in his temple.
verses.4:23: So God routed Jabin, king of Canaan, on that day before the children of Israel.
verses.4:24: And the hand of the children of Israel went on growing heavier and harsher against Jabin, king of Canaan, until they utterly destroyed Jabin, king of Canaan.
verses.5:1: And Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam were saying on that day:
verses.5:2: "A revelation was revealed in Israel; when the people offered themselves willingly, bless the Lord.
verses.5:3: Hear, O kings, and give ear, O satraps; I am for the Lord; I, even I, will sing; I will sing praise to the Lord, the God of Israel.
verses.5:4: O Lord, at Your going forth in Seir, when You departed from the field of Edom, the earth trembled, and heaven dropped dews, and the clouds dropped water.
verses.5:5: Mountains were shaken before the face of the Lord Eloi, this Sinai, before the face of the Lord, the God of Israel.
verses.5:6: In the days of Shamgar the son of Anath, in the days of Jael, they forsook the highways and walked in byways; they walked in crooked paths.
verses.5:7: Mighty men failed in Israel, they failed, until Deborah arose, until a mother arose in Israel.
verses.5:8: They chose new gods, when they fought against the cities of rulers; was a shield and a spear seen among forty thousand in Israel?
verses.5:9: My heart is toward the ordinances for Israel; you who offer yourselves willingly among the people, bless the Lord.
verses.5:10: You who ride upon a female donkey at midday, you who sit upon the judgment seat, and you who walk upon the ways of the councilors along the road—
verses.5:11: declare it from the sound of those who strike up music, in the midst of those who draw water; there they shall give acts of righteousness. O Lord, increase acts of righteousness in Israel; then the people of the Lord went down to the cities.
verses.5:12: Awake, awake, Deborah! Awake, awake, speak a song! Arise, Barak, and take your captivity captive, O son of Abinoam!
verses.5:13: Then a remnant went down to the strong ones; the people of the Lord went down for Him among the mighty ones from me.
verses.5:14: Ephraim uprooted them in Amalek; after you, Benjamin, among your peoples; in me, Machir, they went down searching out, and from Zebulun, those who draw with the rod of the recounting of a scribe.
verses.5:15: And chiefs in Issachar were with Deborah and Barak. So Barak sent forth into the valleys at his feet. To the portions of Reuben there were great ones reaching the heart.
verses.5:16: Why did they sit in the midst of the double load to hear the piping of messengers? For the divisions of Reuben there were great searchings of heart.
verses.5:17: Gilead pitched his tent beyond the Jordan; and Dan, why does he sojourn in ships? Asher sat along the shore of the seas, and by his outlets he shall dwell in tents.
verses.5:18: Zebulun is a people that reproached its soul to death, and Naphtali upon the heights of the field.
verses.5:19: Their kings came, they drew up in battle array; then the kings of Canaan fought in Taanach by the water of Megiddo; a gift of silver they did not take.
verses.5:20: From heaven the stars drew up in battle array; from their paths they drew up in battle array against Sisera.
verses.5:21: The torrent of Kishon swept them away, that torrent of ancient times, the torrent of Kishon; my mighty soul shall trample him down.
verses.5:22: Then the heels of the horse were entangled; in haste his strong ones hastened.
verses.5:23: 'Curse Meroz,' said the angel of the Lord, 'curse her! Cursed is everyone who dwells in her, because they did not come to the help of the Lord, to the help among the mighty.'
verses.5:24: May Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, be blessed among women; above women in tents may she be blessed.
verses.5:25: He asked for water, she gave milk; in a bowl of nobles she brought forth butter.
verses.5:26: Her left hand she stretched out to the peg, and her right hand to the hammer of laborers; and she struck Sisera with the hammer, she drove through his head and smote him, she drove through his temple.
verses.5:27: Between her feet he rolled down, he fell and lay down between her feet; sinking down, he fell; just as he sank down, there he fell, destroyed.
verses.5:28: Through the window the mother of Sisera leaned out, outside the arrow-slit: 'Why has his chariot been put to shame? Why have the feet of his chariots tarried?'
verses.5:29: Her wise princesses answered her, and she herself returned her words to herself:
verses.5:30: 'Will they not find him dividing spoil? Mercifully he will show mercy to the head of a man; spoil of dyed fabrics for Sisera, spoil of dyed fabrics of embroidery, dyed fabrics of embroiderers are they, spoil for his neck.'
verses.5:31: So may all Your enemies perish, O Lord; and may those who love Him be as the going forth of the sun in its strength." And the land had rest for forty years.
verses.6:1: And the sons of Israel did what was evil in the sight of the Lord, and the Lord gave them into the hand of Midian for seven years.
verses.6:2: And the hand of Midian prevailed over Israel; and because of Midian the sons of Israel made for themselves the crevices that are in the mountains, and the caves, and the steep crags.
verses.6:3: And it came to pass, whenever the sons of Israel had sown, that Midian and Amalek would come up, and the sons of the east would come up with them; and they encamped against them,
verses.6:4: and destroyed their produce as far as the entrance to Gaza, and left no sustenance of life in the land of Israel, nor among the flocks a bull or a donkey.
verses.6:5: For they and their livestock would come up, and their tents would arrive, like locusts in multitude, and of them and of their camels there was no number; and they would come into the land of Israel and lay it waste,
verses.6:6: and Israel was greatly impoverished because of Midian.
verses.6:7: And the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord because of Midian.
verses.6:8: And the Lord sent a man, a prophet, to the sons of Israel, and he said to them, "Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: I am He who brought you up from the land of Egypt, and brought you out of the house of your bondage,
verses.6:9: and delivered you out of the hand of Egypt and out of the hand of all who oppressed you, and cast them out from before your face, and gave you their land;
verses.6:10: and I said to you, 'I am the Lord your God; you shall not fear the gods of the Amorite, among whom you shall dwell in their land.' Yet you have not listened to My voice."
verses.6:11: And the angel of the Lord came and sat under the terebinth tree that was in Ephrathah, in the possession of Joash, the father of Esdri; and Gideon his son was beating out wheat in a winepress, to flee from the face of Midian.
verses.6:12: And the angel of the Lord appeared to him and said to him, "The Lord is with you, O mighty one of strength."
verses.6:13: And Gideon said to him, "Pardon me, my lord, and if the Lord is with us, why have these evils found us? And where are all His wondrous deeds which our fathers recounted to us, saying, 'Did not the Lord bring us up from Egypt?' And now He has cast us out and delivered us into the hand of Midian."
verses.6:14: And the angel of the Lord turned to him and said, "Go in this strength of yours, and you shall save Israel out of the hand of Midian. Behold, I have sent you."
verses.6:15: And Gideon said to him, "Pardon me, my lord, by what shall I save Israel? Behold, my thousand has grown weak in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house."
verses.6:16: And the angel of the Lord said to him, "The Lord shall be with you, and you shall strike Midian as one man."
verses.6:17: And Gideon said to him, "If now I have found mercy in your eyes, and you will do for me today all that you have spoken with me,
verses.6:18: do not depart from here until I come to you, and I will bring out the sacrifice and set it before you." And he said, "I myself will sit until you return."
verses.6:19: And Gideon went in and prepared a kid of the goats, and an ephah of flour as unleavened cakes; and the flesh he put in the basket, and the broth he poured into the pot, and he brought them out to him under the terebinth tree, and drew near.
verses.6:20: And the angel of God said to him, "Take the flesh and the unleavened cakes and place them upon that rock, and pour out the broth close by." And he did so.
verses.6:21: And the angel of the Lord stretched out the end of the staff that was in his hand and touched the flesh and the unleavened cakes; and fire went up out of the rock and consumed the flesh and the unleavened cakes; and the angel of the Lord departed from his eyes.
verses.6:22: And Gideon saw that he was the angel of the Lord; and Gideon said, "Alas, my Lord, O Lord! For I have seen the angel of the Lord face to face."
verses.6:23: And the Lord said to him, "Peace be to you; do not fear, you shall by no means die."
verses.6:24: And Gideon built an altar there to the Lord, and called it Peace of the Lord; to this day it is still in Ephrathah, of the father of Esdri.
verses.6:25: And it came to pass on that night that the Lord said to him, "Take the young bull that belongs to your father, and a second bull seven years old, and you shall tear down the altar of Baal that belongs to your father, and the sacred grove that is upon it you shall destroy;
verses.6:26: and you shall build an altar to the Lord your God upon the summit of this Mauek in proper order, and you shall take the second bull and offer up a whole burnt offering with the wood of the sacred grove which you shall utterly destroy."
verses.6:27: And Gideon took ten men from his own servants, and did just as the Lord had spoken to him; and it came to pass, because he feared the house of his father and the men of the city too much to do it by day, that he did it by night.
verses.6:28: And the men of the city rose early in the morning, and behold, the altar of Baal had been torn down, and the sacred grove that was upon it had been destroyed; and they saw the second bull, which he had offered up upon the altar that was built.
verses.6:29: And each man said to his neighbor, "Who has done this thing?" And they inquired and searched, and knew that Gideon the son of Joash had done this thing.
verses.6:30: And the men of the city said to Joash, "Bring out your son, and let him die, because he has torn down the altar of Baal, and because he has destroyed the sacred grove that was upon it."
verses.6:31: And Gideon the son of Joash said to all the men who rose up against him, "Will you now plead for Baal? Or will you save him? Whoever pleads for him, let him be put to death by morning! If he is a god, let him plead for himself, because he has torn down his altar."
verses.6:32: And he called it on that day Arbaal, saying, "Let Baal plead against him, because his altar was torn down."
verses.6:33: And all Midian and Amalek and the sons of the east were gathered together, and they encamped in the valley of Jezreel.
verses.6:34: And the Spirit of the Lord empowered Gideon, and he blew the horn, and Abiezer feared after him.
verses.6:35: And he sent messengers into all Manasseh, and into Asher, and into Zebulun, and Naphtali; and he went up to meet them.
verses.6:36: And Gideon said to God, "If You are saving Israel by my hand, just as You have spoken,
verses.6:37: behold, I am placing the fleece of wool on the threshing floor; if there shall be dew upon the fleece only, and dryness upon all the ground, then I shall know that You will save Israel by my hand, just as You have spoken."
verses.6:38: And it was so; and he rose early on the next day and squeezed out the fleece, and dew dripped from the fleece, a bowl full of water.
verses.6:39: And Gideon said to God, "Do not let Your wrath be kindled against me, and I will speak yet once more; let me indeed test yet once more with the fleece: let dryness be upon the fleece only, and upon all the ground let there be dew."
verses.6:40: And God did so on that night; and there was dryness upon the fleece only, and upon all the ground there was dew.
verses.7:1: And Jerubbaal, who is Gideon, and all the people with him rose early and encamped beside the spring of Arad; and the camp of Midian was to the north of him, from Gabaathamora in the valley.
verses.7:2: And the Lord said to Gideon, "The people who are with you are too many for Me to deliver Midian into their hand, lest Israel boast against Me, saying, 'My hand has saved me.'
verses.7:3: And now, speak in the hearing of the people, saying, 'Who is fearful and timid? Let him turn back and depart from Mount Gilead.'" And twenty-two thousand of the people turned back, and ten thousand remained.
verses.7:4: Then the Lord said to Gideon, "The people are still too many; bring them down to the water, and I will sift them for you there. And it shall be that the one of whom I say to you, 'This one shall go with you,' he shall go with you; and everyone of whom I say to you, 'This one shall not go with you,' he shall not go with you."
verses.7:5: So he brought the people down to the water. And the Lord said to Gideon, "Everyone who laps from the water with his tongue, as a dog laps, you shall set by himself; and likewise everyone who bows down upon his knees to drink."
verses.7:6: And the number of those who lapped with their hand to their mouth was three hundred men, and all the rest of the people bowed down upon their knees to drink water.
verses.7:7: Then the Lord said to Gideon, "By the three hundred men who lapped I will save you and give Midian into your hand; and all the people shall depart, each man to his own place."
verses.7:8: So they took the provisions of the people in their hand, along with their horns. And he sent away every man of Israel, each man to his tent, and retained the three hundred men. Now the camp of Midian was below him in the valley.
verses.7:9: And it came to pass on that night that the Lord said to him, "Arise, go down into the camp, for I have delivered it into your hand.
verses.7:10: Yet if you are afraid to go down, go down, you and Purah your servant, to the camp,
verses.7:11: and you shall hear what they speak; and afterward your hands shall be strengthened, and you shall go down into the camp." Then he and Purah his servant went down to the outpost of the fifty who were in the camp.
verses.7:12: Now Midian and Amalek and all the sons of the east were lying in the valley like locusts in multitude; and their camels were without number, but were as the sand upon the shore of the sea in multitude.
verses.7:13: And Gideon came, and behold, a man was relating a dream to his companion. And he said, "Behold, I have dreamed a dream: and behold, a loaf of barley bread was rolling in the camp of Midian; and it came to the tent and struck it, and it fell, and it turned it upside down, and the tent fell."
verses.7:14: And his companion answered and said, "This is nothing else than the sword of Gideon the son of Joash, a man of Israel! God has delivered Midian and the whole camp into his hand."
verses.7:15: And it came to pass, when Gideon heard the telling of the dream and its interpretation, that he worshiped the Lord. And he returned to the camp of Israel and said, "Arise, for the Lord has delivered the camp of Midian into our hand."
verses.7:16: Then he divided the three hundred men into three companies, and he put horns into the hand of all of them, with empty pitchers and torches inside the pitchers.
verses.7:17: And he said to them, "Watch me and do likewise; and behold, I am going to the outskirts of the camp, and it shall be that just as I do, so you shall do.
verses.7:18: And I will blow the horn, and all of you with me shall blow the horns all around the whole camp, and you shall say, 'For the Lord and for Gideon!'"
verses.7:19: So Gideon and the hundred men who were with him came to the outskirts of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, when they had just roused the watchmen; and they blew the horns and dashed to pieces the pitchers that were in their hands.
verses.7:20: Then the three companies blew the horns and broke the pitchers, and they held the torches in their left hands and the horns in their right hands for blowing; and they cried out, "A sword for the Lord and for Gideon!"
verses.7:21: And every man stood in his place all around the camp; and the whole camp ran, and sounded the alarm, and fled.
verses.7:22: And they blew the three hundred horns, and the Lord set every man's sword against his companion throughout the whole camp; and the camp fled as far as Beth-seedta Garagatha, as far as the border of Abomeoula by Tabbath.
verses.7:23: And the men of Israel from Naphtali, from Asher, and from all Manasseh cried out and pursued after Midian.
verses.7:24: Then Gideon sent messengers throughout all the hill country of Ephraim, saying, "Come down to meet Midian, and seize for yourselves the water as far as Bethera and the Jordan." So every man of Ephraim cried out, and they seized the water beforehand as far as Bethera and the Jordan.
verses.7:25: And they captured the princes of Midian, both Oreb and Zeeb; and they slew Oreb in Sur, and Zeeb they slew in Jakephzeph. And they pursued Midian, and they brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon from beyond the Jordan.
verses.8:1: Now the men of Ephraim said to Gideon, "What is this thing you have done to us, in not calling us when you went to do battle against Midian?" And they contended with him vehemently.
verses.8:2: And he said to them, "What have I done now in comparison with you? Is not the gleaning of Ephraim better than the vintage of Abiezer?
verses.8:3: Into your hand the Lord has delivered the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; and what was I able to do like you?" Then their spirit subsided toward him when he spoke this word.
verses.8:4: Then Gideon came to the Jordan and crossed over, he and the three hundred men who were with him, hungry and pursuing.
verses.8:5: And he said to the men of Succoth, "Please give loaves of bread for food to this people who are at my feet, for they are faint; and behold, I am pursuing after Zebah and Zalmunna, kings of Midian."
verses.8:6: And the princes of Succoth said, "Is the hand of Zebah and Zalmunna now in your hand? We will not give loaves of bread to your army."
verses.8:7: And Gideon said, "Therefore, when the Lord gives Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, then I will thresh your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with the habarkenein."
verses.8:8: Then he went up from there to Penuel and spoke to them in the same manner; and the men of Penuel answered him just as the men of Succoth had answered.
verses.8:9: And Gideon said to the men of Penuel, "When I return in peace, I will tear down this tower."
verses.8:10: Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor, and their camp was with them, about fifteen thousand, all who were left of the entire camp of the foreigners; for those who had fallen were one hundred twenty thousand men who drew the sword.
verses.8:11: And Gideon went up by the way of those who dwell in tents, east of Nabai and Jegebal; and he struck the camp, while the camp felt secure.
verses.8:12: And Zebah and Zalmunna fled; and he pursued after them, and captured the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and threw the entire camp into panic.
verses.8:13: Then Gideon the son of Joash returned from the battle, from above the battle array of Hares.
verses.8:14: And he captured a young man from among the men of Succoth and questioned him; and he wrote down for him the names of the princes of Succoth and their elders, seventy-seven men.
verses.8:15: Then Gideon came to the princes of Succoth and said, "Behold, Zebah and Zalmunna, concerning whom you reproached me, saying, 'Is the hand of Zebah and Zalmunna now in your hand, that we should give loaves of bread to the men who are faint?'"
verses.8:16: And he took the elders of the city with the thorns of the wilderness and the barakeneim, and with them he threshed the men of the city.
verses.8:17: And he overthrew the tower of Penuel and slew the men of the city.
verses.8:18: Then he said to Zebah and Zalmunna, "Where are the men whom you slew at Tabor?" And they said, "As you are, so were they, in the likeness of the son of a king."
verses.8:19: And Gideon said, "They were my brothers and the sons of my mother. As the Lord lives, if you had kept them alive, I would not slay you."
verses.8:20: So he said to Jether his firstborn, "Arise and slay them!" But the youth did not draw his sword, for he was afraid, because he was still young.
verses.8:21: Then Zebah and Zalmunna said, "Arise yourself and fall upon us, for your strength is that of a man." So Gideon arose and slew Zebah and Zalmunna, and took the crescent ornaments that were on the necks of their camels.
verses.8:22: Then the men of Israel said to Gideon, "Lord, rule over us, both you and your son, for you have saved us from the hand of Midian."
verses.8:23: And Gideon said to them, "I will not rule, nor shall my son rule among you; the Lord shall rule over you."
verses.8:24: And Gideon said to them, "I will make a request of you: give me, each man, an earring from his plunder." For they had golden earrings, because they were Ishmaelites.
verses.8:25: And they said, "We will surely give them." So he spread out his cloak, and each man cast there an earring from his plunder.
verses.8:26: And the weight of the golden earrings that he requested was one thousand five hundred gold pieces, besides the crescent ornaments and the pendants, and the garments and purple robes that were upon the kings of Midian, and apart from the collars that were on the necks of their camels.
verses.8:27: And Gideon made it into an ephod and set it up in his city, Ephrathah. And all Israel played the harlot after it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and to his house.
verses.8:28: Thus Midian was subdued before the sons of Israel, and they did not lift up their heads anymore. And the land had rest forty years in the days of Gideon.
verses.8:29: Then Jerubbaal the son of Joash went and dwelt in his own house.
verses.8:30: And Gideon had seventy sons who came forth from his loins, for he had many wives.
verses.8:31: And his concubine was in Shechem, and she also bore him a son, and he called his name Abimelech.
verses.8:32: And Gideon the son of Joash died in his city, and was buried in the tomb of Joash his father in Ephrathah of Abiesdri.
verses.8:33: And it came to pass, as soon as Gideon died, that the sons of Israel turned back and played the harlot after the Baals, and made for themselves a covenant with Baal, that he should be their god.
verses.8:34: And the sons of Israel did not remember the Lord God, who had delivered them from the hand of all who afflicted them on every side.
verses.8:35: Nor did they show mercy to the house of Jerubbaal, who is Gideon, according to all the good that he had done for Israel.
verses.9:1: And Abimelech the son of Jerubbaal went to Shechem to his mother's brothers, and spoke to them and to all the kindred of the house of his mother's father, saying,
verses.9:2: "Speak, I pray, in the ears of all the men of Shechem, 'What is better for you: that seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, should rule over you, or that one man should rule over you? And remember that I am your bone and your flesh.'"
verses.9:3: And his mother's brothers spoke all these words concerning him in the ears of all the men of Shechem; and their heart inclined after Abimelech, for they said, "He is our brother."
verses.9:4: And they gave him seventy pieces of silver from the house of Baal-Berith; and Abimelech hired for himself empty and cowardly men, and they followed after him.
verses.9:5: Then he entered his father's house in Ephrathah and slew his brothers, the sons of Jerubbaal, seventy men, upon one stone. Yet Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, was left, for he hid himself.
verses.9:6: And all the men of Shechem and all the house of Beth-Maalon gathered together, and they went and made Abimelech king by the oak that was found at the pillar in Shechem.
verses.9:7: Now it was told to Jotham; and he went and stood on the summit of Mount Gerizim, and lifted up his voice and wept, and said to them, "Listen to me, men of Shechem, and God will listen to you.
verses.9:8: The trees once went forth to anoint a king over themselves, and they said to the olive tree, 'Reign over us!'
verses.9:9: But the olive tree said to them, 'Should I forsake my richness, by which men will glorify God, and go to sway over the trees?'
verses.9:10: Then the trees said to the fig tree, 'Come, reign over us!'
verses.9:11: But the fig tree said to them, 'Should I forsake my sweetness and my good produce, and go to sway over the trees?'
verses.9:12: Then the trees said to the vine, 'Come, you reign over us!'
verses.9:13: But the vine said to them, 'Should I forsake my wine, which gladdens God and men, and go to sway over the trees?'
verses.9:14: Then all the trees said to the bramble, 'Come, you reign over us!'
verses.9:15: And the bramble said to the trees, 'If in truth you anoint me to reign over you, come, take shelter under my shadow; and if not, let fire come forth from me and devour the cedars of Lebanon!'
verses.9:16: Now therefore, if you have acted in truth and integrity and have made Abimelech king, and if you have done goodness to Jerubbaal and to his house, and if you have dealt with him according to the recompense of his hand—
verses.9:17: for my father fought for you, and cast away his life in the open, and delivered you from the hand of Midian,
verses.9:18: yet you have risen up against my father's house today, and have slain his sons, seventy men, upon one stone, and have made Abimelech, the son of his maidservant, king over the men of Shechem, because he is your brother—
verses.9:19: if then you have acted in truth and integrity with Jerubbaal and with his house on this day, may you rejoice in Abimelech, and may he also rejoice over you!
verses.9:20: But if not, may fire come forth from Abimelech and devour the men of Shechem and the house of Beth-Maalon; and may fire come forth from the men of Shechem and from the house of Beth-Maalon and consume Abimelech!"
verses.9:21: Then Jotham fled and escaped, and went as far as Beer, and dwelt there away from the presence of Abimelech his brother.
verses.9:22: And Abimelech ruled over Israel three years.
verses.9:23: Then God sent forth an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Shechem; and the men of Shechem dealt treacherously with the house of Abimelech,
verses.9:24: in order to bring the injustice against the seventy sons of Jerubbaal and their blood, to lay it upon Abimelech their brother who slew them, and upon the men of Shechem, because they strengthened his hands to slay the brothers.
verses.9:25: And the men of Shechem set men in ambush against him on the tops of the mountains, and they plundered everyone who passed by them along the way; and it was reported to King Abimelech.
verses.9:26: Now Galaad the son of Jobel and his brothers came and passed over into Shechem, and the men of Shechem put their trust in him.
verses.9:27: So they went out into the field, and gathered the grapes of their vineyards and trod them, and held festivities of praise; and they brought them into the house of their god, and ate and spoke and cursed Abimelech.
verses.9:28: And Gaad the son of Jobel said, "Who is Abimelech, and who is the son of Shechem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Jerubbaal, and is not Zebul his overseer, his servant together with the men of Hamor the father of Shechem? And why is it that we should serve him?
verses.9:29: And who would place this people into my hand? Then I would remove Abimelech, and I would say to him, 'Increase your army and come out!'"
verses.9:30: When Zebul, the ruler of the city, heard the words of Galaad the son of Jobel, he himself burned with wrath.
verses.9:31: And he sent messengers to Abimelech in secret, saying, "Behold, Galaad the son of Jobel and his brothers are coming to Shechem, and behold, they are besieging the city against you.
verses.9:32: Now therefore, arise by night, you and the people who are with you, and lie in ambush in the field;
verses.9:33: and it shall be in the morning, as soon as the sun rises, that you shall rise early and rush upon the city; and behold, he and the people who are with him will come out against you, and you shall do to him whatever your hand finds."
verses.9:34: So Abimelech and all the people with him arose by night, and they lay in ambush against Shechem in four companies.
verses.9:35: And Galaad the son of Jobel went out and stood at the entrance of the gate of the city; and Abimelech and the people who were with him rose up from the ambush.
verses.9:36: And Galaad the son of Jobel saw the people, and said to Zebul, "Behold, people are coming down from the tops of the mountains!" And Zebul said to him, "You see the shadow of the mountains as men."
verses.9:37: And Galaad spoke yet again and said, "Behold, people are coming down toward the sea from beside the navel of the land, and another company is coming by the way of Elon-Maonemin."
verses.9:38: Then Zebul said to him, "And where is your mouth, as you spoke, 'Who is Abimelech, that we should serve him?' Is this not the people whom you despised? Go out now, I pray, and do battle against him!"
verses.9:39: So Galaad went out before the men of Shechem and fought against Abimelech.
verses.9:40: And Abimelech pursued him, and he fled from before his face; and many fell wounded as far as the entrance of the gate.
verses.9:41: And Abimelech entered into Arumah; and Zebul drove out Galaad and his brothers, so that they would not dwell in Shechem.
verses.9:42: And it came to pass on the next day that the people went out into the field, and it was told to Abimelech.
verses.9:43: So he took the people and divided them into three companies, and lay in ambush in the field; and he looked, and behold, the people came out from the city, and he rose up against them and struck them down.
verses.9:44: And Abimelech and the commanders who were with him rushed forward and stood at the entrance of the gate of the city, while the two companies rushed upon all who were in the field and struck them down.
verses.9:45: And Abimelech fought against the city all that day; and he captured the city and slew the people who were in it, and tore down the city and sowed it with salt.
verses.9:46: Now when all the men of the towers of Shechem heard of it, they came into the gathering place of Beth-Er-Berith.
verses.9:47: And it was told to Abimelech that all the men of the towers of Shechem were gathered together.
verses.9:48: Then Abimelech went up to Mount Hermon, and all the people who were with him; and Abimelech took the axes in his hand, and cut down a branch of a tree, and lifted it and laid it upon his shoulders, and said to the people who were with him, "What you have seen me do, quickly do as I have done!"
verses.9:49: So every man also cut down a branch, and they followed after Abimelech, and laid them upon the gathering place, and burned the gathering place over them with fire; thus all the men of the tower of Shechem also died, about a thousand men and women.
verses.9:50: Then Abimelech went from Beth-Er-Berith and encamped at Thebez, and captured it.
verses.9:51: But there was a strong tower in the midst of the city, and all the men and women of the city fled there, and shut it behind themselves, and went up to the roof of the tower.
verses.9:52: And Abimelech came up to the tower, and they fought against him; and Abimelech drew near to the door of the tower to burn it with fire.
verses.9:53: Then a certain woman cast a piece of an upper millstone upon Abimelech's head, and crushed his skull.
verses.9:54: And he cried out quickly to the young man who bore his armor, and said to him, "Draw my sword and put me to death, lest they say, 'A woman slew him!'" So his young man pierced him through, and he died.
verses.9:55: And when the men of Israel saw that Abimelech was dead, each man departed to his own place.
verses.9:56: Thus God repaid the wickedness of Abimelech, which he had done to his father in slaying his seventy brothers.
verses.9:57: And all the wickedness of the men of Shechem God returned upon their own head; and upon them came the curse of Jotham the son of Jerubbaal.
verses.10:1: And after Abimelech there arose to save Israel Tola the son of Puah, the son of his father's brother, a man of Issachar; and he dwelt in Shamir in Mount Ephraim.
verses.10:2: And he judged Israel twenty-three years, and he died and was buried in Shamir.
verses.10:3: And after him arose Jair of Gilead, and he judged Israel twenty-two years.
verses.10:4: And he had thirty-two sons who rode on thirty-two colts, and they had thirty-two cities; and they called them the Villages of Jair to this day, in the land of Gilead.
verses.10:5: And Jair died, and was buried in Ramnon.
verses.10:6: Then the children of Israel again did evil in the sight of the Lord, and served the Baalim and the Ashtaroth, and the gods of Arad, and the gods of Sidon, and the gods of Moab, and the gods of the children of Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines; and they forsook the Lord and did not serve Him.
verses.10:7: And the Lord was fiercely angered against Israel, and He sold them into the hand of the Philistines and into the hand of the children of Ammon.
verses.10:8: And they afflicted and crushed the children of Israel in that season for eighteen years—all the children of Israel who were beyond the Jordan, in the land of the Amorites in Gilead.
verses.10:9: Moreover, the children of Ammon crossed over the Jordan to make war against Judah and Benjamin and against Ephraim; and Israel was greatly distressed.
verses.10:10: And the children of Israel cried out to the Lord, saying, "We have sinned against You, because we have forsaken God and served Baalim."
verses.10:11: And the Lord said to the children of Israel, "Was it not from Egypt, and from the Amorites, and from the children of Ammon, and from the Philistines,
verses.10:12: and the Sidonians, and Amalek, and Midian, who afflicted you—and you cried out to Me, and I saved you out of their hand?
verses.10:13: Yet you have forsaken Me and served other gods; therefore I will no longer save you.
verses.10:14: Go and cry out to the gods whom you have chosen for yourselves; let them save you in the time of your distress."
verses.10:15: And the children of Israel said to the Lord, "We have sinned; do to us according to all that is good in Your sight; only deliver us this day."
verses.10:16: So they put away the foreign gods from among them and served the Lord alone; and His soul was grieved over the misery of Israel.
verses.10:17: Then the children of Ammon went up and encamped in Gilead, and the children of Israel gathered together and encamped at the Watchtower.
verses.10:18: And the people, the rulers of Gilead, said, each man to his neighbor, "Who is the man who will begin to make war against the children of Ammon? He shall be ruler over all the inhabitants of Gilead."
verses.11:1: Now Jephthah the Gileadite was exalted in might, and he was the son of a harlot, who bore Jephthah to Gilead.
verses.11:2: And Gilead's wife bore sons to him; and the sons of his wife grew up, and they drove out Jephthah and said to him, "You shall not inherit in the house of our father, for you are the son of a courtesan."
verses.11:3: Then Jephthah fled from the face of his brethren and dwelt in the land of Tob; and worthless men gathered to Jephthah and went out with him.
verses.11:4: And it came to pass, when the children of Ammon made war with Israel,
verses.11:5: that the elders of Gilead went to bring Jephthah from the land of Tob;
verses.11:6: and they said to Jephthah, "Come and be commander for us, and let us make war against the children of Ammon."
verses.11:7: And Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, "Did you not hate me, and drive me out from my father's house, and send me away from you? Why then have you come to me now when you are in need?"
verses.11:8: And the elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "For this very reason we have turned back to you now, that you may go with us and make war against the children of Ammon, and you shall be ruler for us, over all who dwell in Gilead."
verses.11:9: And Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, "If you bring me back to make war against the children of Ammon, and the Lord delivers them before me, shall I indeed be ruler over you?"
verses.11:10: And the elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "Let the Lord be a hearer between us if we do not act according to your word."
verses.11:11: Then Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people set him over themselves as head and as commander; and Jephthah spoke all his words before the Lord in Mizpah.
verses.11:12: Now Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the children of Ammon, saying, "What is there between me and you, that you have come to me to make war in my land?"
verses.11:13: And the king of the children of Ammon said to the messengers of Jephthah, "Because Israel took away my land when he came up out of Egypt, from the Arnon even to the Jabbok and to the Jordan; now therefore restore them in peace, and I will depart."
verses.11:14: And Jephthah again sent messengers to the king of the children of Ammon,
verses.11:15: and said to him, "Thus says Jephthah: Israel did not take away the land of Moab, nor the land of the children of Ammon.
verses.11:16: For when they came up out of Egypt, Israel walked in the wilderness as far as the Sea of Suph and came to Kadesh.
verses.11:17: Then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, 'Let me pass, I pray, through your land'; but the king of Edom did not listen. And he sent also to the king of Moab, and he did not consent. So Israel remained in Kadesh.
verses.11:18: And he journeyed in the wilderness, and went around the land of Edom and the land of Moab, and came on the east of the land of Moab, and they encamped on the other side of the Arnon; and he did not enter within the borders of Moab, for the Arnon was the border of Moab.
verses.11:19: Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, king of Heshbon; and Israel said to him, 'Let us pass, we pray, through your land to our place.'
verses.11:20: But Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his territory; and Sihon gathered all his people together, and they encamped at Jahaz, and he fought against Israel.
verses.11:21: And the Lord God of Israel delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and he struck him down; and Israel possessed all the land of the Amorites who inhabited that land,
verses.11:22: from the Arnon even to the Jabbok, and from the wilderness to the Jordan.
verses.11:23: And now the Lord God of Israel has driven out the Amorites from before His people Israel; and shall you possess them?
verses.11:24: Will you not possess whatever Hamos your god gives you to possess? So all whom the Lord our God has driven out from before us, them we will possess.
verses.11:25: And now, are you indeed any better than Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever contend with Israel, or did he ever wage war against him,
verses.11:26: while he dwelt in Heshbon and in its borders, and in the land of Aroer and in its borders, and in all the cities along the Jordan, for three hundred years? Why then did you not rescue them in that time?
verses.11:27: And now, I myself have not sinned against you, yet you do evil against me in making war with me. May the Lord, the Judge, judge this day between the children of Israel and the children of Ammon."
verses.11:28: However, the king of the children of Ammon did not listen to the words of Jephthah which he sent to him.
verses.11:29: Then the Spirit of the Lord came upon Jephthah, and he passed through Gilead and Manasseh, and passed through the Watchtower of Gilead to the other side of the children of Ammon.
verses.11:30: And Jephthah made a vow to the Lord, and said, "If You will indeed deliver the children of Ammon into my hand,
verses.11:31: then it shall be that whoever comes forth from the door of my house to meet me, when I return in peace from the children of Ammon, shall belong to the Lord; I will offer him up as a burnt offering."
verses.11:32: So Jephthah passed over to the children of Ammon to make war against them, and the Lord delivered them into his hand.
verses.11:33: And he struck them from Aroer until one comes as far as Arnon—twenty cities in number—and as far as Abel-keramim, with a very great slaughter. Thus the children of Ammon were subdued before the children of Israel.
verses.11:34: When Jephthah came to Mizpah to his house, behold, his daughter was coming out to meet him with timbrels and dances; and she was an only child; he had no other son or daughter.
verses.11:35: And it came to pass, when he saw her, that he tore his garments and said, "Alas, alas, my daughter! You have utterly troubled me, and you are in my trouble; for I myself have opened my mouth against you to the Lord, and I cannot turn back."
verses.11:36: And she said to him, "Father, you have opened your mouth to the Lord; do to me according to what has gone out of your mouth, since the Lord has executed vengeance for you upon your enemies, upon the children of Ammon."
verses.11:37: Then she said to her father, "Let my father do this thing: leave me alone for two months, that I may go and go down upon the mountains, and weep over my virginity, I and my companions."
verses.11:38: And he said, "Go." And he sent her away for two months; and she went, she and her companions, and wept over her virginity upon the mountains.
verses.11:39: And it came to pass at the end of the two months that she returned to her father, and he carried out upon her his vow which he had vowed; and she did not know a man. And it became an ordinance in Israel:
verses.11:40: from year to year the daughters of Israel went to lament the daughter of Jephthah of Gilead four days in the year.
verses.12:1: And the men of Ephraim cried out, and crossed over to the north, and said to Jephthah, "Why did you cross over to do battle against the sons of Ammon, and have not called us to go with you? We will burn your house upon you with fire."
verses.12:2: And Jephthah said to them, "I was a man of strife, I and my people, and the sons of Ammon exceedingly; and I cried out to you, and you did not save me from their hand.
verses.12:3: And I saw that you were not a savior, so I put my life in my hand and crossed over to the sons of Ammon, and the Lord gave them into my hand. Why then have you come up against me this day to do battle against me?"
verses.12:4: Then Jephthah gathered together all the men of Gilead and did battle with Ephraim. And the men of Gilead struck down Ephraim, because the fugitives of Ephraim had said, "You are Gilead in the midst of Ephraim and in the midst of Manasseh."
verses.12:5: And Gilead seized the fords of the Jordan of Ephraim. And the fugitives of Ephraim said to them, "Let us cross over." And the men of Gilead said to them, "Are you an Ephraimite?" And he said, "No."
verses.12:6: Then they said to him, "Say now, 'Ear of grain.'" And he did not succeed in speaking it thus; so they laid hold of him and slaughtered him at the fords of the Jordan. And there fell at that time from Ephraim forty-two thousand.
verses.12:7: And Jephthah judged Israel sixty years. Then Jephthah the Gileadite died and was buried in his city in Gilead.
verses.12:8: And after him Ibzan of Bethlehem judged Israel.
verses.12:9: And he had thirty sons and thirty daughters, whom he sent outside, and thirty daughters he brought in from outside for his sons. And he judged Israel seven years.
verses.12:10: Then Ibzan died and was buried in Bethlehem.
verses.12:11: And after him Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel ten years.
verses.12:12: Then Elon the Zebulunite died and was buried in Elon, in the land of Zebulun.
verses.12:13: And after him Abdon the son of Hillel, the Pirathonite, judged Israel.
verses.12:14: And he had forty sons and thirty grandsons who rode on seventy colts. And he judged Israel eight years.
verses.12:15: Then Abdon the son of Hillel, the Pirathonite, died and was buried in Pirathon, in the land of Ephraim, in the mountain of Amalek.
verses.13:1: And the sons of Israel again did evil in the sight of the Lord, and the Lord delivered them into the hand of the Philistines forty years.
verses.13:2: Now there was a certain man from Saral, of the clan of the family of the Danites, and his name was Manoah; and his wife was barren and had borne no children.
verses.13:3: And the Angel of the Lord appeared to the woman and said to her, "Behold, you are barren and have borne no children, yet you shall conceive a son.
verses.13:4: Now therefore, take heed, and do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean;
verses.13:5: for behold, you are with child and shall bear a son. And no iron shall come upon his head, for the child shall be a Nazirite to God from the womb; and he shall begin to save Israel out of the hand of the Philistines."
verses.13:6: So the woman went in and spoke to her husband, saying, "A man of God came to me, and his countenance was like the countenance of an angel of God, exceedingly awesome; and I did not ask him where he was from, nor did he tell me his name.
verses.13:7: And he said to me, 'Behold, you are with child and shall bear a son. Now therefore, do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean, for the child shall be holy to God from the womb until the day of his death.'"
verses.13:8: Then Manoah prayed to the Lord and said, "I pray You, O Lord Adonai, let the man of God whom You sent come to us again and teach us what we shall do for the child who is to be born."
verses.13:9: And God listened to the voice of Manoah, and the Angel of God came again to the woman; and she was sitting in the field, and Manoah her husband was not with her.
verses.13:10: Then the woman hastened and ran and told her husband, and said to him, "Behold, the man who came to me on that day has appeared to me!"
verses.13:11: So Manoah arose and followed his wife, and came to the man and said to him, "Are you the man who spoke to the woman?" And the Angel said, "I am."
verses.13:12: And Manoah said, "Now your word will come to pass; what shall be the ordinance for the child, and his deeds?"
verses.13:13: And the Angel of the Lord said to Manoah, "Of all that I have spoken to the woman, she shall take heed:
verses.13:14: she shall not eat of anything that comes from the vine of wine, nor let her drink wine or strong intoxicating drink, nor let her eat anything unclean; all that I have commanded for him, she shall observe."
verses.13:15: Then Manoah said to the Angel of the Lord, "Let us detain you here, and let us prepare a young goat before you."
verses.13:16: And the Angel of the Lord said to Manoah, "Though you detain Me, I will not eat of your bread; and if you prepare a burnt offering, you shall offer it up to the Lord." For Manoah did not know that He was the Angel of the Lord.
verses.13:17: Then Manoah said to the Angel of the Lord, "What is your name? For may your word come to pass, and we will honor you."
verses.13:18: And the Angel of the Lord said to him, "Why do you ask this—My name? And it is wonderful."
verses.13:19: So Manoah took the young goat and the offering and offered them upon the rock to the Lord, and He acted distinctly, while Manoah and his wife looked on.
verses.13:20: And it came to pass, as the flame went up from above the altar toward heaven, that the Angel of the Lord ascended in the flame of the altar. And Manoah and his wife looked on, and they fell on their faces to the ground.
verses.13:21: And the Angel of the Lord did not appear again to Manoah and to his wife. Then Manoah knew that He was the Angel of the Lord.
verses.13:22: And Manoah said to his wife, "We shall surely die, because we have seen God!"
verses.13:23: But his wife said to him, "If the Lord had desired to put us to death, He would not have accepted a burnt offering and an offering from our hand, nor would He have shown us all these things, nor at this time would He have made us hear these things."
verses.13:24: So the woman bore a son and called his name Samson; and the child grew, and the Lord blessed him.
verses.13:25: And the Spirit of the Lord began to go forth with him in the camp of Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.
verses.14:1: And Samson went down to Timnah, and saw a woman in Timnah of the daughters of the foreigners.
verses.14:2: And he went up and told his father and his mother, and said, "I have seen a woman in Timnah of the daughters of the Philistines; now therefore, get her for me as a wife."
verses.14:3: Then his father and his mother said to him, "Are there no daughters among your brethren, or a woman from all my people, that you go to take a wife from the uncircumcised foreigners?" And Samson said to his father, "Get her for me, for she is right in my eyes."
verses.14:4: Now his father and his mother did not know that it was from the Lord, that He was seeking vengeance from the foreigners. And at that time the foreigners were ruling over Israel.
verses.14:5: So Samson and his father and his mother went down to Timnah; and he came to the vineyard of Timnah, and behold, a young lion came roaring to meet him.
verses.14:6: And the Spirit of the Lord leaped upon him, and he crushed it as one would crush a young goat, though there was nothing in his hands. But he did not tell his father or his mother what he had done.
verses.14:7: Then they went down and spoke to the woman, and she was right in the eyes of Samson.
verses.14:8: And after some days he returned to take her; and he turned aside to see the carcass of the lion, and behold, there was a swarm of bees in the mouth of the lion, and honey.
verses.14:9: And he scooped it out into his hands, and went on his way, walking and eating. And he went to his father and his mother, and gave some to them, and they ate; yet he did not tell them that he had taken the honey out of the mouth of the lion.
verses.14:10: Then his father went down to the woman; and Samson made a banquet there for seven days, for thus the young men do.
verses.14:11: And it came to pass, when they saw him, that they brought thirty guests, and they were with him.
verses.14:12: Then Samson said to them, "I put forth a riddle to you: if you surely declare it during the seven days of the banquet and find it out, I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty robes of clothing;
verses.14:13: but if you are not able to declare it to me, then you shall give me thirty linen cloths and thirty changes of garments." And they said to him, "Put forth the riddle, and we will hear it."
verses.14:14: So he said to them, "What food came forth from the eater, and out of the strong, sweetness?" And they could not declare the riddle for three days.
verses.14:15: And it came to pass on the fourth day that they said to Samson's wife, "Deceive your husband now, and let him declare the riddle to you, lest we burn you and your father's house with fire. Or have you invited us to despoil us?"
verses.14:16: Then Samson's wife wept before him and said, "You only hate me and do not love me, for you have not declared to me the riddle which you put forth to the sons of my people." And Samson said to her, "If I have not declared it to my father and my mother, shall I declare it to you?"
verses.14:17: Now she wept before him for the seven days while their banquet lasted. And it came to pass on the seventh day that he declared it to her, because she troubled him; and she declared it to the sons of her people.
verses.14:18: So the men of the city said to him on the seventh day before the sun rose, "What is sweeter than honey, and what is stronger than a lion?" And Samson said to them, "If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have known my riddle."
verses.14:19: Then the Spirit of the Lord leaped upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon and struck down thirty men of them, and took their garments, and gave the robes to those who had declared the riddle. And Samson burned with wrath, and he went up to his father's house.
verses.14:20: And Samson's wife became the wife of one of his friends with whom he had been a companion.
verses.15:1: And it came to pass after some days, in the days of the wheat harvest, that Samson visited his wife with a young goat; and he said, "I will go in to my wife, into the inner chamber." But her father did not permit him to go in.
verses.15:2: And her father said, "I truly thought that you utterly hated her, so I gave her to one of your companions. Is not her younger sister better than she? Let her now be yours in her place."
verses.15:3: And Samson said to them, "I am blameless even this once regarding the foreigners, for I am doing harm to them."
verses.15:4: So Samson went and caught three hundred foxes; and he took torches, turned tail to tail, placed one torch between the two tails, and bound them.
verses.15:5: And he kindled fire in the torches and sent them forth into the grainfields of the foreigners; and they were burned from the threshing floor even to the standing grain, and even to the vineyard and the olive grove.
verses.15:6: And the foreigners said, "Who has done these things?" And they answered, "Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite, because he took his wife and gave her to one of his companions." Then the foreigners went up and burned her and her father with fire.
verses.15:7: And Samson said to them, "Since you have done thus to her, surely I will take vengeance upon you, and afterward I will cease."
verses.15:8: And he struck them shin upon thigh with a great slaughter; and he went down and dwelt in the cleft of the rock of Etam.
verses.15:9: Then the foreigners went up and encamped in Judah, and they spread out in Leuei.
verses.15:10: And the men of Judah said, "Why have you come up against us?" And the foreigners answered, "We have come up to bind Samson, and to do to him in the manner he has done to us."
verses.15:11: Then three thousand men from Judah went down to the cleft of the rock of Etam, and they said to Samson, "Do you not know that the foreigners rule over us? And what is this that you have done to us?" And Samson said to them, "In the manner they did to me, so have I done to them."
verses.15:12: And they said to him, "We have come down to bind you, to deliver you into the hand of the foreigners." And Samson said to them, "Swear to me that you yourselves will not fall upon me."
verses.15:13: And they spoke to him, saying, "No, we will only bind you securely and deliver you into their hand, and we will by no means put you to death." So they bound him with two new ropes and brought him up from that rock.
verses.15:14: And they came as far as Jawbone, and the foreigners shouted aloud and ran to meet him. Then the Spirit of the Lord leaped upon him, and the ropes that were on his arms became like flax that has been burned with fire, and his bonds melted away from his hands.
verses.15:15: And he found the jawbone of a donkey cast aside, and he stretched out his hand and took it, and struck down with it one thousand men.
verses.15:16: And Samson said, "With the jawbone of a donkey I have utterly blotted them out, for with the jawbone of the donkey I have struck down one thousand men."
verses.15:17: And it came to pass, when he ceased speaking, that he cast the jawbone out of his hand, and he called that place Slaying of a Jawbone.
verses.15:18: Then he became exceedingly thirsty, and he wept to the Lord and said, "You have been pleased to grant by the hand of Your servant this great deliverance, and now I shall die of thirst and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised."
verses.15:19: And God split open the hollow place that is in Jawbone, and water came forth from it; and he drank, and his spirit returned and he revived. Therefore its name was called Spring of the One Who Calls, which is in Jawbone, to this day.
verses.15:20: And he judged Israel in the days of the foreigners twenty years.
verses.16:1: Now Samson went to Gaza, and he saw a harlot there and went in to her.
verses.16:2: And it was reported to the Gazites, saying, "Samson has come here." So they surrounded him and lay in ambush for him all night at the gate of the city, and they kept silent all night, saying, "Wait until the morning dawns, and let us slay him."
verses.16:3: And Samson lay until midnight; and he arose in the middle of the night and took hold of the doors of the city gate together with the two posts, and lifted them up along with the bar and placed them upon his shoulders; and he went up to the summit of the mountain that faces Hebron, and laid them down there.
verses.16:4: And it came to pass after this that he loved a woman in Halsorech, whose name was Delilah.
verses.16:5: And the rulers of the foreigners went up to her and said to her, "Deceive him, and see in what his great strength lies, and by what means we may prevail against him and bind him to humble him; and we will each give you one thousand one hundred pieces of silver."
verses.16:6: So Delilah said to Samson, "Please tell me in what your great strength lies, and with what you may be bound so as to be humbled."
verses.16:7: And Samson said to her, "If they bind me with seven moist bowstrings that have not been spoiled, then I shall become weak and be like any other man."
verses.16:8: So the rulers of the foreigners brought up to her seven moist bowstrings that had not been spoiled, and she bound him with them.
verses.16:9: Now her ambush was sitting in the inner chamber. And she said to him, "The foreigners are upon you, Samson!" But he snapped the bowstrings as one would pull apart a twisted strand of flax when it catches the scent of fire. Thus his strength was not discovered.
verses.16:10: Then Delilah said to Samson, "Behold, you have deceived me and spoken falsehoods to me. Now therefore, tell me with what you may be bound."
verses.16:11: And he said to her, "If they securely bind me with new ropes with which no work has been done, then I shall become weak and be like any other man."
verses.16:12: So Delilah took new ropes and bound him with them, and the men in ambush came out of the inner chamber, and she said, "The foreigners are upon you, Samson!" And he snapped them from his arms like a thread.
verses.16:13: Then Delilah said to Samson, "Behold, you have deceived me and spoken falsehoods to me. Tell me now with what you may be bound." And he said to her, "If you weave the seven locks of my head with the warp and fasten them with the pin into the wall, then I shall become weak like any other man."
verses.16:14: And it came to pass, while he was sleeping, that Delilah took the seven locks of his head, wove them into the warp, and fastened them with the pin into the wall; and she said, "The foreigners are upon you, Samson!" And he awoke from his sleep and pulled out the pin of the web from the wall.
verses.16:15: Then Delilah said to Samson, "How can you say, 'I have loved you,' when your heart is not with me? This third time you have deceived me, and you have not told me in what your great strength lies."
verses.16:16: And it came to pass, when she pressed him with her words all those days and distressed him, that his soul grew faint even to death.
