verses.16:17: So he told her all his heart, and said to her, "Iron has not come upon my head, for I am a holy one of God from my mother's womb. Therefore, if I am shaved, my strength will depart from me, and I shall become weak and be like all other men."
verses.16:18: And when Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart, she sent and called the rulers of the foreigners, saying, "Come up yet this once, for he has told me all his heart." So the rulers of the foreigners came up to her and brought the silver in their hands.
verses.16:19: And Delilah put Samson to sleep upon her knees, and she called a man and shaved off the seven locks of his head; and she began to humble him, and his strength departed from him.
verses.16:20: And Delilah said, "The foreigners are upon you, Samson!" And he awoke from his sleep and said, "I will go out as once and again before, and shake myself free." Yet he did not know that the Lord had departed from him.
verses.16:21: Then the foreigners seized him and gouged out his eyes, and brought him down to Gaza and bound him in bronze fetters; and he was grinding in the prison house.
verses.16:22: And the hair of his head began to grow again after he had been shaved.
verses.16:23: Now the rulers of the foreigners gathered together to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon their god and to rejoice; and they said, "The god has delivered into our hand Samson our enemy."
verses.16:24: And the people saw him and praised their god, saying, "Our god has delivered our enemy into our hand, the one who laid waste our land and who multiplied our slain."
verses.16:25: And when their heart was merry, they said, "Call Samson out of the guardhouse, and let him make sport before us." So they called Samson from the prison house, and he made sport before them; and they struck him on the face, and stationed him between the pillars.
verses.16:26: And Samson said to the young man who held his hand, "Let me go, that I may feel the pillars upon which the house rests, and I will lean against them."
verses.16:27: Now the house was full of men and women, and all the rulers of the foreigners were there; and upon the roof were about seven hundred men and women watching the sport of Samson.
verses.16:28: Then Samson wept to the Lord and said, "Adonai, Lord, remember me now, I pray, and strengthen me yet this once, O God, that I may repay one vengeance upon the foreigners for my two eyes."
verses.16:29: And Samson embraced the two pillars of the house upon which the house stood, and braced himself against them, grasping one with his right hand and one with his left hand.
verses.16:30: And Samson said, "Let my soul die with the foreigners!" And he heaved with might, and the house fell upon the rulers and upon all the people who were in it. So the dead whom Samson slew at his death were more than those whom he had slain in his life.
verses.16:31: Then his brethren and the house of his father came down and took him and brought him up, and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of Manoah his father. And he judged Israel twenty years.
verses.17:1: Now there was a man from Mount Ephraim, and his name was Micah.
verses.17:2: And he said to his mother, "The one thousand one hundred pieces of silver which you took for yourself, and you cursed me and spoke in my ears—behold, the silver is with me; I took it." And his mother said, "Blessed be my son by the Lord."
verses.17:3: So he restored the one thousand one hundred pieces of silver to his mother; and his mother said, "I have wholly consecrated the silver to the Lord from my hand for my son, to make a carved image and a molten image; and now I will return it to you."
verses.17:4: So he restored the silver to his mother; and his mother took two hundred pieces of silver and gave it to a silversmith, who made it into a carved image and a molten image; and it was in the house of Micah.
verses.17:5: And the house of Micah was to him a house of God; and he made an ephod and teraphim, and he filled the hand of one of his sons, who became his priest.
verses.17:6: Now in those days there was no king in Israel; each man did what was upright in his own eyes.
verses.17:7: And there was a young man from Bethlehem, of the clan of Judah, who was a Levite; and he was sojourning there.
verses.17:8: And the man departed from Bethlehem, the city of Judah, to sojourn in whatever place he might find; and he came as far as Mount Ephraim, even to the house of Micah, as he made his journey.
verses.17:9: And Micah said to him, "From where do you come?" And he said to him, "I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, and I am going to sojourn in whatever place I may find."
verses.17:10: And Micah said to him, "Dwell with me, and be to me a father and a priest, and I will give you ten pieces of silver per day, a suit of garments, and the provisions for your livelihood."
verses.17:11: And the Levite went and began to sojourn with the man; and the young man was with him like one of his sons.
verses.17:12: So Micah filled the hand of the Levite, and he became his priest, and he stayed in the house of Micah.
verses.17:13: Then Micah said, "Now I know that the Lord will do good to me, because the Levite has become my priest."
verses.18:1: In those days there was no king in Israel; and in those days the tribe of Dan was seeking for itself an inheritance to dwell in, for until that day no inheritance had fallen to it in the midst of the tribes of Israel.
verses.18:2: And the sons of Dan sent from their clans five men, men of valor, from Zorah and from Eshtaol, to spy out the land and to search it out, and they said to them, "Go and search out the land." And they came as far as Mount Ephraim, to the house of Micah, and they themselves lodged there,
verses.18:3: in the house of Micah. And they recognized the voice of the young man, the Levite, and they turned aside there and said to him, "Who brought you here? And what are you doing in this place? And what do you have here?"
verses.18:4: And he said to them, "Thus and so Micah has done for me, and he hired me, and I have become a priest to him."
verses.18:5: And they said to him, "Inquire now of God, and we shall know whether our way in which we are walking will prosper."
verses.18:6: And the priest said to them, "Go in peace; before the Lord is your way in which you are walking."
verses.18:7: And the five men departed and came to Laish; and they saw the people who were in its midst dwelling in confidence, after the manner of the Sidonians, living quietly; and there was no one deterring or putting to shame any matter in the land, nor any heir extorting treasure; and they were far from the Sidonians, and had no dealings with any man.
verses.18:8: And the five men came to their brethren at Zorah and Eshtaol, and said to their brethren, "Why are you sitting still?"
verses.18:9: And they said, "Arise, and let us go up against them, for we have seen the land, and behold, it is exceedingly good. And are you keeping still? Do not hesitate to go and enter in to inherit the land.
verses.18:10: And whenever you come, you shall enter to a people dwelling in confidence, and the land is broad, for God has given it into your hand—a place where there is no lack of anything that is on the earth."
verses.18:11: And six hundred men of the clans of Dan departed from there, from Zorah and from Eshtaol, girded with weapons of war.
verses.18:12: And they went up and encamped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah. Therefore that place has been called Camp of Dan to this day; behold, it is behind Kiriath-jearim.
verses.18:13: And they passed on from there to Mount Ephraim, and came as far as the house of Micah.
verses.18:14: And the five men who had gone to spy out the land of Laish answered and said to their brethren, "You know that there is in this house an ephod, and teraphim, and a carved image, and a molten image; and now know what you will do."
verses.18:15: And they turned aside there and entered into the house of the young man the Levite, the house of Micah, and asked him concerning his welfare.
verses.18:16: And the six hundred men who were girded with their weapons of war, who were of the sons of Dan, stood by the entrance of the gate.
verses.18:17: And the five men who had gone to spy out the land went up,
verses.18:18: and entered there into the house of Micah, while the priest stood by; and they took the carved image, and the ephod, and the teraphim, and the molten image. And the priest said to them, "What are you doing?"
verses.18:19: And they said to him, "Hold your peace, put your hand upon your mouth, and come with us, and become a father and a priest to us. Is it better for you to be priest to the house of one man, or for you to become priest to a tribe and a house for a clan of Israel?"
verses.18:20: And the heart of the priest was glad, and he took the ephod, and the teraphim, and the carved image, and the molten image, and went into the midst of the people.
verses.18:21: And they turned and departed, and placed the children, and the livestock, and the baggage before them.
verses.18:22: When they had gone far from the house of Micah, behold, Micah and the men who were in the houses beside the house of Micah cried out and overtook the sons of Dan.
verses.18:23: And the sons of Dan turned their faces and said to Micah, "What is the matter with you, that you have cried out?"
verses.18:24: And Micah said, "Because you have taken my carved image which I made, and the priest, and have gone away; and what more do I have? And why is this that you say to me, 'Why do you cry out?'"
verses.18:25: And the sons of Dan said to him, "Do not let your voice be heard among us, lest men bitter of soul fall upon us, and they add life and the life of your house."
verses.18:26: And the sons of Dan went on their way; and Micah saw that they were stronger than he, and he returned to his house.
verses.18:27: And the sons of Dan took what Micah had made, and the priest who belonged to him, and came upon Laish, upon a people living quietly and trusting in confidence; and they struck them with the edge of the sword, and burned the city with fire.
verses.18:28: And there was no deliverer, because it was far from the Sidonians, and they had no dealings with any man; and it was in the valley of the house of Rahab. And they built the city and dwelt in it,
verses.18:29: and they called the name of the city Dan, after the name of Dan their father, who was born to Israel; yet Ulamais was the name of the city formerly.
verses.18:30: And the sons of Dan set up for themselves the carved image; and Jonathan the son of Gershom, the son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land.
verses.18:31: And they set up for themselves the carved image which Micah had made, all the days that the house of God was in Shiloh. And it came to pass in those days that there was no king in Israel.
verses.19:1: And there was a Levite man sojourning on the flanks of Mount Ephraim, and he took for himself a concubine from Bethlehem of Judah.
verses.19:2: And his concubine departed from him, and went away from him to the house of her father, to Bethlehem of Judah; and she was there for the days of four months.
verses.19:3: And her husband arose and went after her to speak to her heart, to bring her back to himself; and his young servant was with him, and a pair of donkeys. And she brought him into the house of her father; and the father of the young woman saw him, and rejoiced to meet him.
verses.19:4: And his father-in-law, the father of the young woman, detained him, and he stayed with him for three days; and they ate and drank, and lodged there.
verses.19:5: And it came to pass on the fourth day that they rose early in the morning, and he stood up to depart; and the father of the young woman said to his son-in-law, "Strengthen your heart with a morsel of bread, and after this you shall go."
verses.19:6: And he sat down, and the two of them ate together and drank; and the father of the young woman said to the man, "Come now, stay the night, and your heart shall be glad."
verses.19:7: And the man arose to depart; yet his father-in-law urged him strongly, so he sat down and lodged there.
verses.19:8: And he rose early in the morning on the fifth day to depart, and the father of the young woman said, "Strengthen your heart, please, and encamp until the day declines." And the two of them ate.
verses.19:9: And the man arose to depart, he and his concubine and his young servant; and his father-in-law, the father of the young woman, said to him, "Behold now, the day has grown weak toward evening; lodge here, and your heart shall be glad, and tomorrow you shall rise early for your journey, and you shall go to your tent."
verses.19:10: And the man was not willing to lodge there, and he arose and departed, and came opposite Jebus, which is Jerusalem; and with him was a pair of saddled donkeys, and his concubine was with him.
verses.19:11: And they came as far as Jebus; and the day was far spent, and the young servant said to his master, "Come now, and let us turn aside into this city of the Jebusites, and lodge in it."
verses.19:12: And his master said to him, "We will not turn aside into a foreign city where there is none of the sons of Israel here, but we will pass on as far as Gibeah."
verses.19:13: And he said to his young servant, "Come, and let us draw near to one of the places, and we shall lodge in Gibeah or in Ramah."
verses.19:14: And they passed on and went their way, and the sun went down on them close by Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin.
verses.19:15: And they turned aside there to go in to lodge in Gibeah; and they went in and sat down in the open square of the city, for there was no man who took them into a house to lodge.
verses.19:16: And behold, an old man was coming from his work out of the field at evening; and the man was from Mount Ephraim, and he was sojourning in Gibeah, whereas the men of the place were sons of Benjamin.
verses.19:17: And he lifted up his eyes and saw the wayfaring man in the open square of the city; and the old man said, "Where are you going, and from where do you come?"
verses.19:18: And he said to him, "We are passing from Bethlehem of Judah to the flanks of Mount Ephraim; I am from there, and I went as far as Bethlehem of Judah, and I am going to my own house; and there is no man who takes me into a house.
verses.19:19: Yet indeed there is straw and fodder for our donkeys, and there is bread and wine for me and for the maidservant and for the young man with your servants; there is no lack of anything."
verses.19:20: And the old man said, "Peace be to you; only let every need of yours be upon me, only in the open square you shall by no means lodge."
verses.19:21: And he brought him into his house, and made a place for the donkeys; and they washed their feet, and ate and drank.
verses.19:22: Now while they were making their hearts glad, behold, men of the city, sons of lawless men, surrounded the house, pounding on the door; and they spoke to the old man, the master of the house, saying, "Bring out the man who came into your house, that we may know him."
verses.19:23: And the man, the master of the house, went out to them and said, "No, brethren, please do not do evil, since this man has entered into my house; do not commit this folly.
verses.19:24: Behold, here are my virgin daughter and his concubine. I will bring them out, and humble them, and do to them what is good in your eyes; but to this man you shall not do this act of folly."
verses.19:25: And the men were not willing to listen to him; so the man seized his concubine and brought her out to them outside; and they knew her, and abused her all night until morning, and they let her go as the morning broke.
verses.19:26: And the woman came toward daybreak, and fell down at the door of the house where her husband was, until it grew light.
verses.19:27: And her husband arose in the morning and opened the doors of the house, and went out to go on his way; and behold, the woman, his concubine, was lying fallen at the doors of the house, with her hands upon the threshold.
verses.19:28: And he said to her, "Arise, and let us depart." Yet she did not answer, for she was dead. And he took her upon the donkey, and went to his own place.
verses.19:29: And he took the sword and laid hold of his concubine, and cut her into twelve pieces, and sent them throughout all the territory of Israel.
verses.19:30: And it came to pass that everyone who saw it said, "Such a thing has never happened nor been seen from the day the sons of Israel came up from the land of Egypt even to this day; take counsel for yourselves concerning it, and speak."
verses.20:1: And all the sons of Israel went out, and the congregation was assembled as one man, from Dan even to Beersheba and the land of Gilead, to the Lord at Mizpah.
verses.20:2: And all the tribes of Israel stood before the Lord in the assembly of the people of God, four hundred thousand men on foot who drew the sword.
verses.20:3: And the sons of Benjamin heard that the sons of Israel had gone up to Mizpah. And the sons of Israel came and said, "Speak, where did this wickedness happen?"
verses.20:4: And the Levite, the husband of the woman who was murdered, answered and said, "I and my concubine came to Gibeah of Benjamin to lodge for the night.
verses.20:5: And the men of Gibeah rose up against me and surrounded the house against me by night. They intended to murder me, and they violated my concubine, and she died.
verses.20:6: And I took hold of my concubine and cut her into pieces, and sent her throughout all the territory of the inheritance of the sons of Israel, because they have committed depravity and outrage in Israel.
verses.20:7: Behold, all of you, sons of Israel, give for yourselves a word and counsel there."
verses.20:8: And all the people rose up as one man, saying, "We will not depart, each man to his tent, nor will we return, each man to his house.
verses.20:9: And now this is the matter that shall be done to Gibeah: we will go up against it by lot.
verses.20:10: However, we will take ten men out of a hundred throughout all the tribes of Israel, and a hundred out of a thousand, and a thousand out of ten thousand, to gather provisions to bring them to Gibeah of Benjamin, to do to it according to all the outrage that it has committed in Israel."
verses.20:11: And every man of Israel was gathered together against the city as one man.
verses.20:12: And the tribes of Israel sent men throughout all the tribe of Benjamin, saying, "What is this wickedness that has taken place among you?
verses.20:13: And now hand over the men, the sons of lawless men, who are in Gibeah, and we will put them to death and purge away wickedness from Israel." But the sons of Benjamin were not willing to listen to the voice of their brethren, the sons of Israel.
verses.20:14: And the sons of Benjamin gathered together from their cities to Gibeah to go out to battle against the sons of Israel.
verses.20:15: And the sons of Benjamin were mustered on that day from the cities, twenty-three thousand men who drew the sword, besides the inhabitants of Gibeah, who were mustered as seven hundred men,
verses.20:16: chosen out of all the people, ambidextrous; all these were slingers of stones at a hair and did not miss.
verses.20:17: And the men of Israel, besides Benjamin, were mustered: four hundred thousand men who drew the sword; all these were men of battle.
verses.20:18: And they arose and went up to Bethel, and inquired of God. And the sons of Israel said, "Who shall go up for us first to battle against the sons of Benjamin?" And the Lord said, "Judah shall go up first as leader."
verses.20:19: And the sons of Israel arose in the morning and encamped against Gibeah.
verses.20:20: And every man of Israel went out to battle against Benjamin, and they joined battle with them at Gibeah.
verses.20:21: And the sons of Benjamin came out from Gibeah, and cut down twenty-two thousand men in Israel to the ground on that day.
verses.20:22: And the men of Israel strengthened themselves, and again joined battle in the place where they had joined battle on the first day.
verses.20:23: And the sons of Israel went up and wept before the Lord until evening, and inquired of the Lord, saying, "Shall we again draw near to battle against the sons of Benjamin, our brethren?" And the Lord said, "Go up against them."
verses.20:24: And the sons of Israel drew near against the sons of Benjamin on the second day.
verses.20:25: And the sons of Benjamin went out to meet them from Gibeah on the second day, and cut down eighteen thousand more men of the sons of Israel to the ground.
verses.20:26: And all the sons of Israel and all the people went up and came to Bethel, and they wept and sat there before the Lord, and fasted on that day until evening, and offered up burnt offerings and complete offerings before the Lord,
verses.20:27: for there was the ark of the covenant of the Lord God,
verses.20:28: and Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, stood before it in those days. And the sons of Israel inquired of the Lord, saying, "Shall we yet again go out to battle against the sons of Benjamin, our brethren, or shall we cease?" And the Lord said, "Go up, for tomorrow I will deliver them into your hands."
verses.20:29: And the sons of Israel set ambushes around Gibeah.
verses.20:30: And the sons of Israel went up against the sons of Benjamin on the third day, and joined battle against Gibeah as at the former times.
verses.20:31: And the sons of Benjamin went out to meet the people and were drawn away from the city, and began to strike down and slay from the people, as at the former times, on the highways—one of which goes up to Bethel and one to Gibeah in the field—about thirty men in Israel.
verses.20:32: And the sons of Benjamin said, "They are falling before us as at the first." And the sons of Israel said, "Let us flee and draw them away from the city to the highways." And they did so.
verses.20:33: And every man rose up from his place, and they joined battle at Baal Tamar; and the ambush of Israel advanced from its place, from Maraagabe.
verses.20:34: And ten thousand chosen men out of all Israel came over against Gibeah, and the battle was fierce; and they did not know that calamity was coming upon them.
verses.20:35: And the Lord struck Benjamin before the sons of Israel; and the sons of Israel destroyed twenty-five thousand one hundred men of Benjamin on that day. All these drew the sword.
verses.20:36: And the sons of Benjamin saw that they were struck down; and the men of Israel gave ground to Benjamin, because they trusted in the ambush that they had set against Gibeah.
verses.20:37: And as they withdrew, the ambush moved; and they pushed forward against Gibeah, and the ambush poured forth and struck the city with the edge of the sword.
verses.20:38: And the sons of Israel had a sign with the ambush of the battle, that they should raise up a signal of smoke from the city.
verses.20:39: And the sons of Israel saw that the ambush had already seized Gibeah, and they stood firm in the battle. And Benjamin began to strike down and slay among the men of Israel about thirty men, for they said, "Again they are surely falling before us, as in the first battle."
verses.20:40: And the signal rose higher above the city like a pillar of smoke; and Benjamin looked behind him, and behold, the complete destruction of the city ascended to heaven.
verses.20:41: And the men of Israel turned back; and the men of Benjamin hastened, for they saw that calamity had come upon them.
verses.20:42: And they turned before the sons of Israel toward the way of the wilderness and fled; and the battle overtook them, and those from the cities were destroying them in their midst.
verses.20:43: And they cut Benjamin to pieces, and pursued him from Noua hard on his heels as far as opposite Gibeah toward the rising of the sun.
verses.20:44: And eighteen thousand men fell from Benjamin, all of these men of valor.
verses.20:45: And the remainder turned and fled into the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, and the sons of Israel gleaned five thousand men from among them; and the sons of Israel went down after them as far as Gedan, and struck down two thousand men of them.
verses.20:46: And all who fell of Benjamin on that day were twenty-five thousand men who drew the sword, all of these men of valor.
verses.20:47: And the remainder, six hundred men, turned and fled into the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, and dwelt at the rock of Rimmon four months.
verses.20:48: And the sons of Israel turned back against the sons of Benjamin, and struck them with the edge of the sword, from the city of Methla even to the livestock, and even to everything that was found in all the cities; and the cities that were found they burned with fire.
verses.21:1: Now the sons of Israel had sworn in Mizpah, saying, "No man from among us shall give his daughter to Benjamin for a wife."
verses.21:2: And the people came to Bethel, and sat there until evening before God; and they lifted up their voice and wept with great weeping.
verses.21:3: And they said, "Why, O Lord God of Israel, has this come to pass, that one tribe should be missing from Israel today?"
verses.21:4: And it came to pass on the next day that the people rose early, and built an altar there, and offered up burnt offerings and complete offerings.
verses.21:5: And the sons of Israel said, "Who from all the tribes of Israel did not come up in the assembly to the Lord?" For the oath was great against those who had not come up to the Lord to Mizpah, saying, "He shall surely be put to death."
verses.21:6: And the sons of Israel were moved with compassion toward Benjamin their brother, and said, "One tribe has been cut off today from Israel.
verses.21:7: What shall we do for wives for them, those who remain, who are left? And we have sworn by the Lord not to give them any of our daughters for wives."
verses.21:8: And they said, "Which one from the tribes of Israel did not come up to the Lord to Mizpah?" And behold, no man had come to the camp from Jabesh Gilead, to the assembly.
verses.21:9: And the people were mustered, and there was not a man there from the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead.
verses.21:10: And the congregation sent twelve thousand men there from the sons of valor, and commanded them, saying, "Go and strike the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead with the edge of the sword.
verses.21:11: And this you shall do: every male and every woman who has known lying with a male you shall devote to destruction, but the virgins you shall keep alive." And they did so.
verses.21:12: And they found among the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead four hundred young virgins, who had not known a man by lying with a male; and they brought them to the camp at Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan.
verses.21:13: And the whole congregation sent word and spoke to the sons of Benjamin at the rock of Rimmon, and called them to peace.
verses.21:14: And Benjamin returned to the sons of Israel at that time, and the sons of Israel gave them the women whom they had kept alive from the daughters of Jabesh Gilead; and it pleased them so.
verses.21:15: And the people were moved with compassion for Benjamin, because the Lord had made a breach among the tribes of Israel.
verses.21:16: And the elders of the congregation said, "What shall we do for wives for those who remain, since women have been destroyed from Benjamin?"
verses.21:17: And they said, "There must be an inheritance for the survivors of Benjamin, and a tribe shall not be blotted out from Israel.
verses.21:18: For we shall not be able to give them wives from our daughters, because we have sworn among the sons of Israel, saying, 'Cursed is the one who gives a wife to Benjamin.'"
verses.21:19: And they said, "Behold now, there is a feast of the Lord in Shiloh from year to year, which is on the north of Bethel, toward the rising of the sun on the road that goes up from Bethel to Shechem, and on the south of Lebonah."
verses.21:20: And they commanded the sons of Benjamin, saying, "Go, lie in ambush in the vineyards,
verses.21:21: and watch; and behold, if the daughters of the inhabitants of Shiloh come out to dance in the dances, then you shall come out from the vineyards and seize for yourselves, every man a wife from the daughters of Shiloh, and go to the land of Benjamin.
verses.21:22: And it shall come to pass, when their fathers or their brothers come to contend with you, that we will say to them, 'Show mercy to us concerning them, because we did not take each man his wife in the battle, for you yourselves did not give them to them; as a lot, incur guilt.'"
verses.21:23: And the sons of Benjamin did so, and took wives according to their number from the dancers whom they had seized; and they went and returned to their inheritance, and built the cities and dwelt in them.
verses.21:24: And the sons of Israel departed from there at that time, every man to his tribe and to his kindred, and they went out from there, every man to his inheritance.
verses.21:25: Now in those days there was no king in Israel; every man did what was upright in his own sight.

notes.1:10: Codex Vaticanus adds "and Hebron came out to meet them" and "the offspring of Anak," reads Kariarboxepher (apparently conflating Kiriath-arba with Kiriath-sepher), and reads Achinaan for Hebrew Ahiman; similarly, vv. 12–13 read Aza (Achsah in v. 15) and v. 17 reads Sephek and Anathema (Hormah).
notes.1:15: The Greek reads "redemption of water" (lytrosis), reflecting an understanding of the Hebrew word for "springs" from the root meaning "to redeem," and adds "according to her heart."
notes.1:18: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which reports that Judah took Gaza, Ashkelon, and Ekron, the Septuagint states that Judah did not inherit them and adds Ashdod.
notes.1:19: Codex Vaticanus reads "because Rechab had given orders to them," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "because they had chariots of iron."
notes.1:35: Codex Vaticanus translates Mount Heres as "the potsherd mountain," adds "in which are the bears and in which are the foxes," and reads Myrsinon ("Myrtle-grove") and Thalabin for Aijalon and Shaalbim; compare also the distinct Greek place names Balak, Kedron, Domana, Dalaph, Aschazi, Chebda, Naei, Ereo, and Beth-anach in vv. 27–33.
notes.2:1: The Septuagint translates Hebrew Bochim as "the Place of Weeping" (plural "Places of Weeping" in v. 5), adds "and to Bethel, and to the house of Israel" and "Thus says the Lord," and in v. 2 adds "nor shall you worship their gods, but you shall shatter their carved images."
notes.2:3: The Greek renders the Hebrew expression as "for distresses" (synochas) rather than "in your sides," reading the Hebrew consonants as "distresses" or "adversaries."
notes.2:21: Codex Vaticanus reads "left in the land. And He left them" where the Hebrew reads "left when he died"; in v. 23, the Greek also uses the future tense ("will leave").
notes.3:3: The Septuagint refers to the Philistines throughout Judges as 'the foreigners' (allophyloi) and to their five territories as 'satrapies' (satrapiai). It also reads 'Mount Hermon' rather than 'Mount Baal-hermon.'
notes.3:15: The Greek renders the Hebrew idiom for 'left-handed' ('restricted in his right hand') as amphoterodexion, 'ambidextrous.'
notes.3:17: Codex Vaticanus describes Eglon as 'a very handsome man' (asteios sphodra), contrasting with the Masoretic Text's 'a very fat man.'
notes.3:24: The Greek literally reads 'emptying his feet,' a Septuagint euphemism for relieving oneself (compare the Masoretic idiom 'covering his feet').
notes.3:31: Codex Vaticanus reads 'Deinach' instead of Hebrew 'Anath,' and 'the plowshare of the oxen' (arotropodi) instead of 'oxgoad.' Earlier in 3:26, Vaticanus likewise has 'Seteirotha' for Hebrew 'Seirah.'
notes.4:5: Codex Vaticanus reads 'Bama' rather than the Masoretic Text's 'Ramah.'
notes.4:8: The closing clause ('for I do not know the day on which the Lord prospers the angel with me') is a distinctive Septuagint addition not present in the Masoretic Text.
notes.4:11: The Greek translates the Hebrew place name Zaanannim by its root meaning as 'the oak of the covetous' (dryos pleonektounton).
notes.4:17: Codex Vaticanus includes 'the companion' (hetairou) alongside 'Heber,' reflecting a double rendering of the Hebrew name Cheber both as a proper name and as a common noun.
notes.4:21: Codex Vaticanus reads exestos eskotothe ('stunned, fainted away,' literally 'was darkened'), describing Sisera's collapse rather than his prior sleep and weariness as in the Masoretic Text.
notes.5:1: The Greek text reads ἦσαν ("were ... saying"), though the uncial ΗΣΑΝ of Codex Vaticanus may also be read as ᾖσαν ("sang").
notes.5:2: Codex Vaticanus spells the verb ἀκουσιασθῆναι, an orthographic variant of ἑκουσιασθῆναι ("to offer oneself willingly"; compare ἑκουσιαζόμενοι in 5:9).
notes.5:5: Codex Vaticanus reads Κυρίου Ἐλωεί ("the Lord Eloi"), preserving a transliterated divine title not present in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.5:16: Codex Vaticanus reads συρισμοῦ ἀγγέλων ("the piping of messengers"), differing from the Hebrew text's "piping for the flocks."
notes.5:30: Codex Vaticanus translates the Hebrew expression for captive maidens through the root meaning "mercy," yielding οἰκτείρμων οἰκτειρήσει ("mercifully he will show mercy").
notes.6:11: Codex Vaticanus reads Ἐφραθά ("Ephrathah") for Ophrah and renders the clan name Abiezrite literally as πατρὸς τοῦ Ἐσδρεί ("the father of Esdri"; cf. 6:24).
notes.6:26: Codex Vaticanus transliterates the Hebrew noun for "stronghold" as a proper name, τοῦ Μαουὲκ τούτου ("this Mauek").
notes.6:31: Codex Vaticanus attributes this speech to Γεδεὼν υἱὸς Ἰωάς ("Gideon the son of Joash"), whereas the Hebrew text attributes it to Joash.
notes.6:32: Codex Vaticanus reads neuter αὐτό ("it") and the name Ἀρβάαλ ("Arbaal"), corresponding to Hebrew Jerubbaal, followed by a passive verb ("was torn down").
notes.6:34: Codex Vaticanus reads ἐφοβήθη ("feared") where the Hebrew text reads "was called out" or "rallied."
notes.7:1: Codex Vaticanus reads "Arad" (corresponding to Hebrew Harod) and transliterates Hebrew "the hill of Moreh" as the single place name "Gabaathamora."
notes.7:11: Codex Vaticanus reads "of the fifty," reflecting a different vocalization of the Hebrew consonants rendered "armed men" in the Masoretic Text.
notes.7:22: Codex Vaticanus preserves the distinct place-name forms "Beth-seedta Garagatha" and "Abomeoula" (corresponding to "Beth-shittah toward Zererah" and "Abel-meholah" in the Masoretic Text); likewise in verse 24 it reads "Bethera" for "Beth-barah."
notes.7:25: Codex Vaticanus transliterates the Hebrew phrases "at the rock of Oreb" and "at the winepress of Zeeb" as the place names "Sur" and "Jakephzeph."
notes.8:7: Codex Vaticanus transliterates the Hebrew term for briers or threshing-thorns as "habarkenein" here and "barakeneim" in verse 16.
notes.8:13: Codex Vaticanus reads "from above the battle array of Hares," where the Masoretic Text has "from the ascent of Heres."
notes.8:18: Codex Vaticanus translates the Hebrew interrogative as "Where are the men?" rather than "What kind of men were they?"
notes.8:26: Codex Vaticanus gives the weight as "one thousand five hundred gold pieces," compared with "one thousand seven hundred shekels of gold" in the Masoretic Text.
notes.8:33: Codex Vaticanus renders Hebrew "Baal-berith" as "a covenant with Baal." Earlier, in verses 27 and 32, it reads "Ephrathah" (and "Abiesdri") for "Ophrah" (and "the Abiezrites"), and in verse 32 reads "in his city" rather than "in a good old age."
notes.9:5: Codex Vaticanus reads "Ephrathah" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Ophrah."
notes.9:6: Codex Vaticanus reads "Beth-Maalon" (MT "Beth-Millo") and describes the landmark as "the oak that was found at the pillar," reflecting a double rendering of the Hebrew term for the pillar.
notes.9:26: Codex Vaticanus names Abimelech's rival "Galaad the son of Jobel" throughout this narrative (spelled "Gaad" in 9:28), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Gaal the son of Ebed."
notes.9:27: "Festivities of praise" translates the Greek transliteration elloulim (from Hebrew hillulim, vintage celebrations); Codex Vaticanus also reads "ate and spoke" where the Hebrew has "ate and drank."
notes.9:48: Codex Vaticanus reads "Mount Hermon" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Mount Zalmon," and in 9:46 and 9:50 refers to the Shechemite sanctuary as "Beth-Er-Berith."
notes.10:1: Codex Vaticanus reads "the son of his father's brother" (i.e., his uncle), rendering Hebrew Dodo as a common noun rather than a personal name.
notes.10:4: Codex Vaticanus uniquely reads "thirty-two" for Jair's sons, colts, and cities (where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "thirty"), and translates the place name Havvoth-jair as "the Villages of Jair."
notes.10:5: Codex Vaticanus reads "Ramnon," corresponding to "Kamon" in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.10:6: Codex Vaticanus reads "Arad," corresponding to "Aram" (Syria) in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.10:12: Codex Vaticanus reads "Midian," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Maon" (the Maonites).
notes.10:17: Codex Vaticanus translates Mizpah as "the Watchtower" here and in 11:29 ("the Watchtower of Gilead"), while transliterating it as "Mizpah" in 11:11 and 11:34.
notes.11:2: Codex Vaticanus reads hetairas ("a courtesan"), differing by one letter from heteras ("another woman"), which corresponds to the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.11:16: "the Sea of Suph" reflects the Greek transliteration thalasses Seiph of Hebrew Yam Suph ("Sea of Reeds," traditionally rendered "the Red Sea").
notes.11:24: Codex Vaticanus spells the Moabite deity's name as "Hamos," corresponding to "Chemosh" in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.11:26: Codex Vaticanus reads "along the Jordan," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "along the Arnon."
notes.11:33: Codex Vaticanus reads "as far as Arnon," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "as far as Minnith."
notes.11:35: Codex Vaticanus explicitly includes "against you" in Jephthah's lament ("opened my mouth against you to the Lord").
notes.12:1: The Greek reads eis borran ("to the north"), translating the Hebrew place-name Zaphon according to its literal directional meaning.
notes.12:4: Codex Vaticanus places "the fugitives of Ephraim" as the subject of "said," whereas the Hebrew text is commonly understood as part of the taunt ("You Gileadites are fugitives of Ephraim").
notes.12:6: The Greek translates the Hebrew password Shibboleth into its literal meaning (Stachys, "ear of grain") rather than transliterating it, and omits the mispronounced form Sibboleth.
notes.12:7: Codex Vaticanus reads hexekonta ("sixty") years here, in contrast to the six years of the Hebrew Masoretic Text and Codex Alexandrinus.
notes.13:2: Codex Vaticanus spells the town Saral here, whereas it appears as Saraa (Zorah) in verse 25.
notes.13:5: The Greek reads sideros ("iron") rather than "razor," rendering the Hebrew term broadly.
notes.13:14: Codex Vaticanus reads the masculine pronoun auto ("for him" / "him"), referring to the promised child, whereas the Hebrew text reads feminine ("her").
notes.13:19: Codex Vaticanus translates the Hebrew with diechorisen ("separated/set apart"), reflecting an alternate sense of the Hebrew root rather than "acted wondrously."
notes.13:25: Codex Vaticanus reads synekporeuesthai auto ("to go forth with him"), in contrast to the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "to stir/impel him."
notes.14:1: Here and in verses 3-4, the Greek uses allophyloi ("foreigners"), the Septuagint's regular designation for the Philistines, while verse 2 uses the transliteration Phylistieim ("Philistines").
notes.14:8: Codex Vaticanus reads "in the mouth" here and in verse 9, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "in the carcass/body."
notes.14:15: Codex Vaticanus reads "on the fourth day" (fitting the three days of verse 14), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "on the seventh day."
notes.14:18: Codex Vaticanus reads pro tou anateilai ton helion ("before the sun rose"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text is commonly rendered "before the sun went down."
notes.15:3: Greek allophyloi ("foreigners") is the Septuagint's consistent designation for the Philistines throughout Judges.
notes.15:9: Codex B transliterates Hebrew Lehi as Leuei here, whereas in verses 14, 17, and 19 it translates the place name directly as Siagon ("Jawbone").
notes.15:15: Greek ekrerimmenen ("cast aside") differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which reads "fresh."
notes.15:16: Codex B renders the Hebrew wordplay ("heaps upon heaps") with the emphatic Greek idiom exaleiphon exeleipsa autous ("I have utterly blotted them out").
notes.16:4: Codex B merges Hebrew nahal Soreq ("valley of Sorek") into the single place name Halsorech and spells Delilah's name Daleida.
notes.16:13: Codex B preserves the fuller clause "and fasten them with the pin into the wall, then I shall become weak like any other man," which is absent from the Masoretic Text.
notes.16:17: Codex B reads sideros ("iron") rather than "razor" and translates Hebrew "Nazirite" as hagios theou ("a holy one of God").
notes.16:27: Codex B reads "about seven hundred" (hos heptakosioi), whereas the Masoretic Text and Codex Alexandrinus read "about three thousand."
notes.16:28: Codex B transliterates Hebrew Adonai directly as vocative Adonaie ("Adonai, Lord") and uses eklausen ("wept") rather than "called out" (as also in 15:18).
notes.17:2: Codex B reads "which you took for yourself, and you cursed me," differing from the Masoretic Text's passive "which were taken from you, about which you uttered a curse."
notes.17:5: Codex B reads "the house of Micah" (rather than "the man Micah" as in the Masoretic Text); "filled the hand" (eplerosen ten cheira) is the literal consecration idiom meaning to ordain or install as priest (also in v. 12).
notes.17:10: Codex B reads eis hemeran ("per day"), whereas the Masoretic Text has layyamim ("per year").
notes.18:7: The Greek text of Codex Vaticanus uniquely reads "nor any heir extorting treasure," reflecting a reading of the Hebrew consonants as "treasure" rather than "restraint" or "dominion."
notes.18:8: In the Greek text the five scouts speak to their brethren ("Why are you sitting still?"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has the brethren asking the scouts what they report.
notes.18:25: The Greek literally reads "fall upon us, and they add life and the life of your house," using the verb "add" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has a similar-sounding verb meaning "take away."
notes.18:28: The Greek renders the place name as "the house of Rahab," corresponding to Beth-rehob in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.18:29: "Ulamais" is a Septuagint-distinct place name formed by transliterating the Hebrew word for "however" together with the city name "Laish."
notes.19:2: Codex Vaticanus reads "departed from him," whereas other Greek manuscripts read "became angry with him" and the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "was unfaithful against him."
notes.19:8: Codex Vaticanus uses the unusual military verb meaning "encamp" or "go on campaign," standing where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "linger" or "tarry."
notes.19:18: The Greek text reads "to my own house," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "to the house of the Lord."
notes.19:21: Codex Vaticanus reads "made a place for the donkeys," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text states that he gave fodder to the donkeys.
notes.19:28: The Greek text explicitly includes "for she was dead," a clause absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.20:6: The Greek text uses the transliteration "zema" (from Hebrew "zimmah," depravity or lewdness) paired with "apoptoma" (literally "downfall" or "lapse," here rendered "outrage").
notes.20:15: Codex Vaticanus reads "twenty-three thousand" for the mustered Benjaminites, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "twenty-six thousand."
notes.20:33: "Maraagabe" is a Septuagint proper-name transliteration of the Hebrew phrase meaning "open ground of Gibeah" or "meadow of Gibeah."
notes.20:43: "Noua" is a Septuagint place-name rendering of the Hebrew term for "resting place" (or "Nohah").
notes.20:48: "Methla" (like "Gedan" in 20:45) preserves a distinctive Septuagint proper-name reading where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "an entire/inhabited city" (and "Gidom" in 20:45).
notes.21:4: Greek teleias literally means "complete offerings," Codex Vaticanus's distinctive rendering of the Hebrew peace or fellowship offerings (reflecting the Hebrew root meaning "whole" or "complete").
notes.21:11: Codex Vaticanus includes the explicit directive "but the virgins you shall keep alive. And they did so," while omitting the phrase "with the women and the little ones" in 21:10, differing from the Masoretic Text.
notes.21:14: Codex Vaticanus reads "and it pleased them so" (kai eresen autois houtos), whereas the Masoretic Text reports that they did not find enough wives for them.
notes.21:22: Codex Vaticanus reads "with you" (pros hymas, vs. Masoretic "to us") and ends with the difficult reading "as a lot, incur guilt" (hos kleros plemmelesate), likely an inner-Greek corruption of hos kairos plemmelesete ("at this time you would be guilty").
notes.21:25: Codex Vaticanus reads "in his own sight" (enopion autou, literally "before him") rather than the Masoretic idiom "in his own eyes."
